spelling.text: あげる・もらう・くれる

patterns.title: Giving & receiving verbs (あげる / もらう / くれる)
definition: Express giving/receiving. あげる = I/my side give to someone; もらう = receive from someone; くれる = someone gives to me/my side.

spelling.text: わたしは 友だちに 花を あげました。

definition: I gave flowers to my friend.

spelling.text: で

patterns.title: で (location of action / means)
definition: Marks the location where an action takes place, or the means / method used.

spelling.text: レストランで昼ごはんを食べます。

definition: I eat lunch at the restaurant.

spelling.text: です

patterns.title: です (polite copula "is / am / are")
definition: Polite copula that turns a noun or na-adjective into a polite predicate — the polite form of だ.

spelling.text: 私は学生です。

definition: I am a student.

spelling.text: へ

patterns.title: へ (direction toward)
definition: Direction particle. Indicates the direction of motion — similar to に but emphasises the direction rather than the endpoint.

spelling.text: 日本へ行きます。

definition: I am going to Japan.

spelling.text: が

patterns.title: が (subject marker)
definition: Subject marker. Introduces the grammatical subject — often new information, existence, or answers to "who / what" questions.

spelling.text: 猫がいます。

definition: There is a cat.

spelling.text: から

patterns.title: から (from / because)
definition: Marks a starting point (time or place), or a reason / cause ("because").

spelling.text: 九時から五時まで働きます。

definition: I work from nine to five.

spelling.text: 〜にする・〜くする
〜くする／〜にする
い-Adj(〜く) する / な-Adj・N(〜に) する

patterns.title: 〜にする / 〜くする — make X (intentional change)
definition: Expresses the subject intentionally changing something to a different state or quality; use にする with na-adjectives and nouns, くする with i-adjectives.
Someone intentionally changes a state. い-adj → 〜くする; な-adj / noun → 〜にする. The intentional counterpart of 〜なる (natural change).

Expresses a person deliberately changing the state of something, using an adjective. With i-adjectives the ending becomes く, with na-adjectives and nouns it becomes に, then する is added. The agent is a person, and it takes the transitive frame 〜を…くする / にする.

spelling.text: 部屋を綺麗にしてから出かけた。

definition: I tidied the room before going out. (intentional change → にする)

spelling.text: すみません、音を 小さく して ください。

definition: Excuse me, please turn the volume down (make it smaller).

spelling.text: エアコンをつけて、部屋を涼しくしました。

definition: I turned on the AC and made the room cool.

spelling.text: まで

patterns.title: まで (until / up to)
definition: Marks the endpoint of a time span or spatial range — "until / up to / as far as".

spelling.text: 九時から五時まで働きます。

definition: I work from nine until five.

spelling.text: も

patterns.title: も (also / too)
definition: Means "also / too". Replaces は, が, or を when adding "me too" / "this too" / "that too" to a prior statement.

spelling.text: 私も学生です。

definition: I am also a student.

spelling.text: に

patterns.title: に (time / destination / indirect object)
definition: Multi-use particle marking a point in time, a destination, an indirect object, or a location of existence.

spelling.text: 七時に起きます。

definition: I get up at seven.

spelling.text: の

patterns.title: の (possessive / noun modifier)
definition: Links two nouns. Expresses possession, belonging, attribute, or descriptive relationship between them.

spelling.text: これは私の本です。

definition: This is my book.

spelling.text: 名詞修飾

patterns.title: Noun modification (clause + noun)
definition: Place a plain-form verb/adjective clause before a noun to describe it: 〜する人, 友だちにもらった本.

spelling.text: これは 友だちに もらった 本です。

definition: This is the book I received from my friend.

spelling.text: 〜たり〜たりする
Vたり、Vたり する

patterns.title: 〜たり〜たりする (do things like ~ and ~)
definition: List a few representative actions out of several: "do things like A and B". Shows examples, not an exhaustive list.
Picks out about two representative actions from among several, implying there are others. The sentence is closed with する.

spelling.text: 日よう日は 本を 読んだり、音楽を 聞いたり します。

definition: On Sundays I do things like read books and listen to music.

spelling.text: 休みの日は、本を読んだり、音楽を聞いたりします。

definition: On my days off I do things like read books and listen to music.

spelling.text: と

patterns.title: と (with / and / quotation)
definition: Marks accompaniment ("with"), exhaustive listing ("and" between nouns), or a quotation ("that …").

spelling.text: 友達と映画を見ます。

definition: I will watch a movie with my friend.

spelling.text: 〜ませんでした／〜なかった

patterns.title: Verb past-negative (〜ませんでした / 〜なかった)
definition: Says an action "did not happen" in the past. Polite: 〜ませんでした; plain: 〜なかった.

spelling.text: きのうは 学校へ 行きませんでした。

definition: I didn't go to school yesterday.

spelling.text: は

patterns.title: は (topic marker)
definition: Topic marker. Introduces what the sentence is about — "as for X" / "speaking of X".

spelling.text: 私は田中です。

definition: I am Tanaka. (As for me, [I am] Tanaka.)

spelling.text: を

patterns.title: を (direct object marker)
definition: Direct-object marker. Also marks the location traversed (with motion verbs) or the point departed from.

spelling.text: パンを食べます。

definition: I eat bread.

spelling.text: 〜や〜（など）

patterns.title: 〜や (non-exhaustive list "and (among others)")
definition: Particle joining nouns in a NON-exhaustive list — "A and B (among others)". Often paired with など at the end. Contrast with と which implies an exhaustive list.

spelling.text: 冷蔵庫にパンやたまごがあります。

definition: There is bread and eggs (among other things) in the fridge.

spelling.text: あります

patterns.title: あります (inanimate existence)
definition: Polite verb expressing the existence of inanimate things, plants, and abstract concepts — "there is / I have".

spelling.text: 机の上に本があります。

definition: There is a book on the desk.

spelling.text: 〜でしょう

patterns.title: 〜でしょう (probability / confirmation "probably / right?")
definition: Polite conjecture or confirmation. With statement: "probably / I think …". With rising intonation: "right? / isn't it?". Attaches to plain verb / adjective / noun (drop だ). Plain-form counterpart is だろう.

spelling.text: 明日は雨でしょう。

definition: It will probably rain tomorrow.

spelling.text: います

patterns.title: います (animate existence)
definition: Polite verb expressing the existence of animate beings — people, animals, insects. "There is / there are".

spelling.text: 公園に子供がいます。

definition: There are children in the park.

spelling.text: 〜ません

patterns.title: 〜ません (polite non-past negative verb form)
definition: Polite non-past negative form — "do not / will not" politely.

spelling.text: お酒を飲みません。

definition: I do not drink alcohol.

spelling.text: 〜ます

patterns.title: 〜ます (polite non-past verb form)
definition: Polite non-past affirmative form of a verb — roughly "[do / will do] politely".

spelling.text: 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。

definition: I drink coffee every morning.

spelling.text: 〜ない

patterns.title: 〜ない form (plain negative verb)
definition: Plain negative form of a verb — the casual counterpart of 〜ません. Serves as the base for many N5 patterns (〜ないで, 〜なくて, 〜なければ).

spelling.text: 私は肉を食べない。

definition: I don't eat meat.

spelling.text: 〜なければなりません / 〜なくてはいけません

patterns.title: 〜なければなりません (obligation "must do")
definition: Double-negative construction meaning "must / have to …". Literally "if-not-do, it-will-not-do." The two forms (〜なければなりません / 〜なくてはいけません) are essentially interchangeable in N5 contexts.

spelling.text: 明日早く起きなければなりません。

definition: I have to wake up early tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜なくてもいい / 〜なくてもいいです
〜なくてもいい

patterns.title: 〜なくてもいい ("don't have to / not necessary")
definition: Negative-permissive pattern: "don't have to …" / "it is OK not to …". Negative counterpart of 〜てもいい.
Turn the negative into 〜なくて and add もいい to mean 'you don't have to ~ / it's OK not to ~'.

spelling.text: 明日は来なくてもいいです。

definition: You don't have to come tomorrow.

spelling.text: 明日は休みだから、早く起きなくてもいいです。

definition: 'Tomorrow is a holiday, so you don't have to get up early.'

spelling.text: 辞書形（普通形・非過去肯定）

patterns.title: Dictionary / plain non-past verb form
definition: The base form of a verb as it appears in the dictionary — plain, non-past, affirmative. The casual counterpart of 〜ます, and the required form before many patterns (〜つもり, 〜と思う, 〜こと, relative clauses, 〜前に).

spelling.text: 毎日コーヒーを飲む。

definition: I drink coffee every day.

spelling.text: 〜た（普通過去）

patterns.title: 〜た form (plain past verb)
definition: Plain past form of a verb. Formed with the same rules as the て-form, except the final ending is た / だ instead of て / で. Casual counterpart of 〜ました.

spelling.text: 昨日、映画を見た。

definition: I watched a movie yesterday.

spelling.text: 〜ないでください

patterns.title: 〜ないでください (negative request "please do not")
definition: Verb-ない form + で + ください. Polite negative request — "please do not …".

spelling.text: ここでタバコを吸わないでください。

definition: Please do not smoke here.

spelling.text: 〜て

patterns.title: て-form (verb connective form)
definition: The connective form of a verb. Serves as the base for many N5 expressions — linking clauses, requests (〜てください), progressive (〜ている), permission (〜てもいい) etc.

spelling.text: 朝起きて、ご飯を食べます。

definition: I wake up in the morning and eat breakfast.

spelling.text: 〜ている

patterns.title: 〜ている (progressive action or resulting state)
definition: Verb-て + いる. Expresses (1) an action in progress right now, or (2) a resulting state — which meaning applies depends on the verb. Polite form: います.

spelling.text: 今、本を読んでいます。

definition: I am reading a book right now.

spelling.text: 〜てから

patterns.title: 〜てから ("after doing …")
definition: Verb-て + から. Marks "after doing X, Y" — emphasises sequence and that the second action depends on the first being complete.

spelling.text: 宿題をしてから、テレビを見ます。

definition: After doing my homework, I watch TV.

spelling.text: 〜てください

patterns.title: 〜てください (polite request "please do")
definition: Polite request form built on the て-form of a verb + ください — asks the listener to do something politely.

spelling.text: 窓を開けてください。

definition: Please open the window.

spelling.text: 〜てもいいです
〜てもいい

patterns.title: 〜てもいいです (permission "may / is OK to")
definition: Verb-て + も + いい(です). Grants permission ("you may / it is OK to"), or — as 〜てもいいですか — asks for permission.
Verb て-form + もいい(です) expresses permission: 'it's OK to ~'. In question form it asks for permission.

spelling.text: ここで写真を撮ってもいいです。

definition: You may take photos here.

spelling.text: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。

definition: 'May I take photos here?'

spelling.text: 〜てはいけない / 〜てはいけません
〜てはいけない

patterns.title: 〜てはいけません (prohibition "must not")
definition: Verb-て + は + いけない / いけません. Expresses strong prohibition — "it is not OK to …" / "you must not …".
Verb て-form + はいけない/はいけません expresses prohibition: 'you must not ~'. Common for stating rules.

spelling.text: ここで泳いではいけません。

definition: You must not swim here.

spelling.text: ここで写真を撮ってはいけません。

definition: 'You must not take photos here.'

spelling.text: 〜がほしい

patterns.title: 〜がほしい (want something [noun])
definition: Noun + が + ほしい. Expresses the speaker's desire for a concrete or abstract thing. For desiring to DO an action, use 〜たい instead. First-person only — others use ほしがる.

spelling.text: 新しい車がほしいです。

definition: I want a new car.

spelling.text: 〜が上手 / 〜が下手

patterns.title: 〜が上手 / 〜が下手 (good at / bad at)
definition: な-adjectives expressing skill level. The skill or object takes が. 上手 = skilled at; 下手 = unskilled at. Culturally, 上手 for one's own skills sounds boastful — 得意 is more natural — but N5 teaches 上手 / 下手 as the basic pair.

spelling.text: 田中さんは日本語が上手です。

definition: Tanaka-san is good at Japanese.

spelling.text: 〜が好き / 〜が嫌い

patterns.title: 〜が好き / 〜が嫌い (like / dislike)
definition: な-adjectives for liking and disliking. The object being liked / disliked takes が (not を).

spelling.text: 私は寿司が好きです。

definition: I like sushi.

spelling.text: 〜くない

patterns.title: い-adjective (non-past negative)
definition: Non-past negative of い-adjectives. The final い changes to くない: 高い → 高くない / 高くないです / 高くありません.

spelling.text: この部屋は広くないです。

definition: This room is not spacious.

spelling.text: 〜い（形容詞）

patterns.title: い-adjective (non-past affirmative)
definition: Base form of adjectives ending in い. Polite form adds です directly: 高い → 高いです.

spelling.text: この本は面白いです。

definition: This book is interesting.

spelling.text: 〜かった

patterns.title: い-adjective (past affirmative)
definition: Past affirmative of い-adjectives. The final い changes to かった: 高い → 高かった / 高かったです.

spelling.text: 昨日のテストは難しかったです。

definition: Yesterday's test was difficult.

spelling.text: いい

patterns.title: いい (irregular conjugation — uses よい stem)
definition: The adjective いい ("good") is a colloquial form of よい. When conjugating (past / negative / adverbial), you MUST revert to the よ- stem: 良かった, 良くない, 良く.

spelling.text: 今日は天気がいいです。

definition: The weather is good today.

spelling.text: 〜じゃない / 〜じゃありません

patterns.title: な-adjective (non-past negative)
definition: Non-past negative of な-adjectives. Uses じゃない (plain) / じゃありません (polite) — same as nouns.

spelling.text: この問題は簡単じゃありません。

definition: This problem is not simple.

spelling.text: 〜（な）＋です

patterns.title: な-adjective (non-past affirmative)
definition: Base form of な-adjectives. Takes だ (plain) / です (polite) when used as a predicate; takes な before a noun it modifies.

spelling.text: この町は静かです。

definition: This town is quiet.

spelling.text: 〜でした / 〜だった

patterns.title: な-adjective (past affirmative)
definition: Past affirmative of な-adjectives. Takes だった (plain) / でした (polite) — same as nouns.

spelling.text: 昨日の試験は簡単でした。

definition: Yesterday's exam was easy.

spelling.text: どんな + 名詞

patterns.title: どんな ("what kind of [noun]")
definition: Attributive question word: "what kind of [noun]". Must be immediately followed by a noun.

spelling.text: どんな音楽が好きですか。

definition: What kind of music do you like?

spelling.text: どうして

patterns.title: どうして (question-word "why")
definition: Question-word asking for a reason — "why / for what reason". Synonymous with なぜ; more colloquial. Can stand alone as a short "Why?".

spelling.text: どうして日本語を勉強していますか。

definition: Why are you studying Japanese?

spelling.text: か

patterns.title: か (question particle)
definition: Sentence-final question particle. Turns a statement into a yes/no or open question.

spelling.text: これは本ですか。

definition: Is this a book?

spelling.text: こちら / そちら / あちら / どちら

patterns.title: Polite demonstratives (this way / that way / that way / which way — also this person / which one)
definition: Polite demonstratives. Refer to a direction ("this way"), a person (polite introduction), or "which of two" in questions. Casual equivalents are こっち / そっち / あっち / どっち.

spelling.text: こちらへどうぞ。

definition: This way, please.

spelling.text: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ

patterns.title: Demonstrative pronouns for places (here / there / over-there / where)
definition: Place pronouns. ここ = speaker's location, そこ = listener's location, あそこ = far from both, どこ = where (question).

spelling.text: ここは図書館です。

definition: This (place) is a library.

spelling.text: この / その / あの / どの + 名詞

patterns.title: Attributive demonstratives (this / that / that / which + NOUN)
definition: Demonstrative determiners — must be immediately followed by a noun. Counterparts of これ / それ / あれ / どれ when used attributively.

spelling.text: この人は田中さんです。

definition: This person is Tanaka-san.

spelling.text: これ / それ / あれ / どれ

patterns.title: Demonstrative pronouns for things (this / that / that-over-there / which)
definition: Pronouns pointing to things. これ = near speaker, それ = near listener, あれ = far from both, どれ = which (question).

spelling.text: これは私の本です。

definition: This is my book.

spelling.text: 何か／誰か

patterns.title: 何か / 誰か (something / someone)
definition: Question-word + か marks an indefinite referent: 何か = "something", 誰か = "someone", どこか = "somewhere". Positive counterpart of nanimo-daremo-neg.

spelling.text: 何か食べましたか。

definition: Did you eat something?

spelling.text: 何も／誰も + 否定

patterns.title: 何も / 誰も + negative (nothing / no one)
definition: Question-word + も + negative forms a total-negation: 何も = "nothing", 誰も = "no one", どこにも = "nowhere". Only works with negative predicates.

spelling.text: 今日は何も食べませんでした。

definition: I didn't eat anything today.

spelling.text: でも

patterns.title: でも (sentence-initial "but / however")
definition: Sentence-initial "but / however". Used at the start of a new sentence to contrast with the previous. More casual than しかし; the sentence-level counterpart of けど / が.

spelling.text: お腹がすきました。でも、食べる時間がありません。

definition: I'm hungry. But, I don't have time to eat.

spelling.text: 〜が（逆接）

patterns.title: 〜が (clause connector "but / however")
definition: Clause-connecting が meaning "but / however". Used in formal speech and writing. More formal than けど; essentially identical meaning.

spelling.text: 日本語は難しいですが、面白いです。

definition: Japanese is difficult, but interesting.

spelling.text: 〜けど

patterns.title: 〜けど (but / however — casual)
definition: Casual "but / however / although". Attaches to plain or polite form. Colloquial variant of けれども / けれど / が. Also used as a soft preface without strong contrast.

spelling.text: 日本語は難しいけど、面白いです。

definition: Japanese is difficult, but interesting.

spelling.text: ね

patterns.title: ね (confirmation / agreement tag)
definition: Sentence-final tag meaning "right? / isn't it?" — seeks agreement or confirmation from the listener.

spelling.text: 今日は寒いですね。

definition: It's cold today, isn't it?

spelling.text: 普通形（な形・N は〜な）＋ので
〜ので

patterns.title: 〜ので (because; reason)
definition: States a reason or cause. More objective and softer than から, so it suits requests, refusals, and polite situations.
Conjunction marking an objective / polite reason. Softer and more formal than から. Commonly used to preface a request. Na-adjectives and nouns take なので.

spelling.text: 頭が痛いので、今日は早く帰ります。

definition: I have a headache, so I'm going home early today.

spelling.text: 雨が降っているので、タクシーで行きます。

definition: It's raining, so I'll go by taxi.

spelling.text: それから

patterns.title: それから ("and then / after that")
definition: Sequential connective: "and then / after that". Links two sentences, emphasising order or addition. More conversational than そして.

spelling.text: 朝、コーヒーを飲みました。それから、学校に行きました。

definition: In the morning, I drank coffee. Then, I went to school.

spelling.text: よ

patterns.title: よ (emphatic / informing tag)
definition: Sentence-final tag meaning "I'm telling you / you know" — informs the listener of new information or emphasises the speaker's stance.

spelling.text: あの店はおいしいですよ。

definition: That restaurant is delicious, you know.

spelling.text: XよりYのほうが〜

patterns.title: ほうが (preference / "Y is more … than X")
definition: Comparative preference: "Y is more … than X". Also serves as the base for 〜ほうがいい (had better). Inverse of yori-comparison.

spelling.text: コーヒーより紅茶のほうが好きです。

definition: I like tea more than coffee.

spelling.text: 〜の中で〜が一番〜

patterns.title: 一番 (superlative "the most")
definition: Superlative: "Out of [group], X is the most …". 一番 alone also modifies an adjective/adverb for "the most".

spelling.text: クラスの中で田中さんが一番背が高いです。

definition: Tanaka-san is the tallest in the class.

spelling.text: 〜ませんか

patterns.title: 〜ませんか (polite invitation "would you like to …?")
definition: A polite invitation dressed as a negative question. Literally "won't you …?" but used to propose a shared activity more softly than ましょう.

spelling.text: 一緒に映画を見ませんか。

definition: Would you like to watch a movie together?

spelling.text: 〜ましょう

patterns.title: 〜ましょう (volitional "let's / shall we")
definition: Polite volitional built on the ます-stem: "let's …" / "shall we …". Also expresses the speaker's own intention.

spelling.text: 一緒に昼ごはんを食べましょう。

definition: Let's have lunch together.

spelling.text: もう／まだ

patterns.title: もう / まだ ("already" / "still / not yet")
definition: もう = "already" (completion): もう食べました = "I've already eaten". まだ = "still / not yet" — affirmative form means "still doing", negative form means "not yet done". Taught as a contrasting pair.

spelling.text: もう昼ごはんを食べましたか。

definition: Have you already had lunch?

spelling.text: 〜になる・〜くなる
〜になる / 〜くなる
い-Adj(〜く) なる / な-Adj・N(〜に) なる

patterns.title: 〜になる / 〜くなる — become X (natural/spontaneous change)
definition: Expresses natural or spontaneous change into a new state or quality (intransitive in meaning); use になる with na-adjectives and nouns, くなる with i-adjectives.
The verb なる ("become") expresses a change of state. Attached as 〜になる to nouns and な-adjectives, or 〜くなる to い-adjectives.

Expresses that the state of something or someone changes naturally or as a result. With i-adjectives the ending becomes く, with na-adjectives and nouns it becomes に, then なる is added. It is an intransitive expression focusing on the change itself, not on a person's intention.

spelling.text: 3月になると、桜が咲き始める。

definition: When it becomes March, the cherry blossoms begin to bloom. (natural seasonal change → になる)

spelling.text: 日本語が上手になりました。

definition: I have become good at Japanese.

spelling.text: 秋になって、朝晩が寒くなりました。

definition: Autumn came and the mornings and evenings have gotten cold.

spelling.text: 〜すぎる・〜すぎだ
〜すぎる
V[ます-stem] / Adj語幹 + すぎる
〜すぎだ
〜すぎです

patterns.title: Excessive action or state / Noun-like evaluation of excess
definition: Conjugating verb: add すぎる to a verb’s ます-stem or an adjective stem (drop final い or な) to describe an excessive degree. すぎる conjugates as an ichidan verb.
Noun-like evaluation: an expression such as 食べすぎ can be followed by だ or です to evaluate the excess, rather than conjugating すぎる as a verb.
Excess commonly has a negative implication, but conversational expressions such as かわいすぎる can instead express enthusiastic approval: “too cute!”

spelling.text: 昨夜は飲みすぎて、今朝は頭が痛い。

definition: I drank too much last night and have a headache this morning.

spelling.text: 昨日、食べすぎました。

definition: I ate too much yesterday.

spelling.text: ゆうべお酒を飲みすぎて、頭が痛いです。

definition: I drank too much last night, so my head hurts.

spelling.text: それは食べすぎです。

definition: That's too much eating / That's overeating.

spelling.text: かわいすぎる！

definition: Too cute!

spelling.text: 〜たい

patterns.title: 〜たい (desire "want to do")
definition: Built on the verb ます-stem: "want to …". Used for the speaker's own desire; conjugates like an い-adjective (たくない / たかった).

spelling.text: 日本に行きたいです。

definition: I want to go to Japan.

spelling.text: 〜と思う / 〜と思います
〜と思う

patterns.title: 〜と思う (opinion / conjecture "I think that …")
definition: Plain-form clause + と + 思う / 思います. Reports the speaker's opinion, belief, or conjecture — "I think that …".
Expresses the speaker's opinion or conjecture. Uses plain form + と思う / と思います. The clause before と is always plain form.

spelling.text: 日本語は面白いと思います。

definition: I think Japanese is interesting.

spelling.text: 明日は雨が降ると思います。

definition: I think it will rain tomorrow.

spelling.text: とても

patterns.title: とても (degree adverb "very")
definition: Degree adverb meaning "very / extremely". Modifies adjectives and stative predicates. More conversational than 非常に (a more formal alternative).

spelling.text: この本はとても面白いです。

definition: This book is very interesting.

spelling.text: 〜つもりだ
〜つもり
V辞書形／Vない形 + つもりだ
Vた形 + つもりだ
〜つもりで

patterns.title: Intention / Self-perception / Assumed state
definition: Intention: V dictionary-form or Vない-form + つもりだ expresses an intention or plan to do or not do something.
Self-perception: a completed action or a state before つもり describes what the speaker considers to be true, which may differ from reality. Vた-form + つもり can mean thinking that one has done something.
Assumed role or state: 〜つもりで describes acting from an imagined perspective or as though a state were true; it does not necessarily express a plan to make that state real.

spelling.text: 来年、日本語の試験を受けるつもりです。

definition: I intend to take the Japanese language exam next year.

spelling.text: 来年、日本に行くつもりです。

definition: I intend to go to Japan next year.

spelling.text: 来年、日本で働くつもりです。

definition: A firm plan to work in Japan next year.

spelling.text: 日本語を勉強するつもりです。

definition: I intend to study Japanese.

spelling.text: 日本語を勉強したつもりです。

definition: I consider myself to have studied Japanese / I thought I had studied Japanese.

spelling.text: 先生になったつもりで説明してください。

definition: Explain it as though you were a teacher.

spelling.text: 勉強したつもりだったけど、全然覚えていなかった。

definition: I thought I'd studied, but I hadn't remembered a thing.

spelling.text: XはYより〜です

patterns.title: XはYより (X is more … than Y)
definition: Comparison construction: "X is more [adjective] than Y". より marks the thing being compared against.

spelling.text: 東京は大阪より大きいです。

definition: Tokyo is bigger than Osaka.

spelling.text: 〜本（ほん／ぼん／ぽん）

patterns.title: Long-cylindrical counter (〜本)
definition: Counter for long, cylindrical objects (pens, bottles, bananas) and also phone calls, films, roads. Reading alternates between ほん / ぼん / ぽん depending on the preceding number.

spelling.text: ビールを三本ください。

definition: Please give me three bottles of beer.

spelling.text: 〜枚（まい）

patterns.title: Flat-object counter (〜枚)
definition: Counter for flat, thin objects: paper, cloth, plates, tickets, CDs, stamps. Readings are regular: いちまい, にまい, さんまい, よんまい, ごまい …

spelling.text: 切符を二枚買いました。

definition: I bought two tickets.

spelling.text: 〜人（にん）

patterns.title: People counter (〜人)
definition: Counter for people. Readings for 1 and 2 are irregular: 一人 ひとり, 二人 ふたり. From 3 onward it is [number] + にん: 三人 さんにん, 四人 よにん (irregular — not しにん), 五人 ごにん ...

spelling.text: 家族は四人です。

definition: My family has four people.

spelling.text: 〜冊（さつ）

patterns.title: Bound-volume counter (〜冊)
definition: Counter for bound volumes: books, magazines, notebooks, dictionaries. Readings: いっさつ, にさつ, さんさつ, よんさつ, ごさつ …

spelling.text: 本を三冊買いました。

definition: I bought three books.

spelling.text: 〜つ

patterns.title: General counter (〜つ — 1-10 only)
definition: Native-Japanese general counter usable for most objects (apples, ideas, issues, servings). Only covers 1-10; from 11 onward, use 数字 or a specific counter.

spelling.text: りんごを三つください。

definition: Please give me three apples.

spelling.text: 〜月〜日

patterns.title: Month + day (〜月〜日)
definition: Month and day date expression. Month = [number] + がつ (irregulars: 4月 しがつ, 7月 しちがつ, 9月 くがつ). Day 1-10 irregular (ついたち / ふつか / みっか / よっか / いつか / むいか / なのか / ようか / ここのか / とおか). 14日 じゅうよっか, 20日 はつか, 24日 にじゅうよっか.

spelling.text: 私の誕生日は三月十日です。

definition: My birthday is March 10th.

spelling.text: 〜曜日

patterns.title: Days of the week (〜曜日)
definition: Day-of-week expressions. All end in 〜曜日 (ようび). 月曜日 (Mon) · 火曜日 (Tue) · 水曜日 (Wed) · 木曜日 (Thu) · 金曜日 (Fri) · 土曜日 (Sat) · 日曜日 (Sun).

spelling.text: 今日は水曜日です。

definition: Today is Wednesday.

spelling.text: 〜前に / 〜の前に

patterns.title: 〜前に ("before doing / before [noun]")
definition: Verb dictionary form + 前に OR Noun + の + 前に. Marks that the main clause happens BEFORE the referenced action or moment.

spelling.text: 寝る前に歯を磨きます。

definition: I brush my teeth before sleeping.

spelling.text: 〜分（ふん／ぷん）

patterns.title: Minute marker (〜分)
definition: Minute marker. Reading alternates between ふん and ぷん depending on the preceding number (rendaku).

spelling.text: 七時十五分に家を出ます。

definition: I leave home at 7:15.

spelling.text: 〜時（じ）

patterns.title: Hour marker (〜時)
definition: Hour marker "o'clock". [Number] + 時. Irregular readings: 4 → よじ (not しじ), 7 → しちじ, 9 → くじ (not きゅうじ).

spelling.text: 今、九時です。

definition: It is nine o'clock now.

spelling.text: 〜とき / 〜時

patterns.title: 〜とき ("when …")
definition: Verb / adjective plain form, or Noun + の + とき. Marks the time point at which the main-clause action or state applies.

spelling.text: 寒いとき、コートを着ます。

definition: When it's cold, I wear a coat.

spelling.text: 〜ばいいです

patterns.title: 〜ba ii desu — 'you just need to ~' / asking how to do something
definition: 'You just have to ~' — points to the method/condition that solves the problem; in a question it asks how to do something.

spelling.text: この薬は一日二回飲めばいいです。

definition: You just need to take this medicine twice a day.

spelling.text: 〜んです / 〜のです

patterns.title: 〜n desu / 〜no desu — giving or asking for an explanation
definition: Used to give or ask for the reason / background behind a situation; softens and explains. Plain form + んです.

spelling.text: どうして昨日休んだんですか。

definition: Why did you take yesterday off?

spelling.text: 〜たらどうか
〜たらどうですか

patterns.title: How about doing X? / Why don't you X?
definition: A suggestion or recommendation to the listener to try a course of action. 「〜てみたらどうか」 is synonymous. Generally gentle advice, though in context can carry a mild implication of 'why haven't you already?'
Suggests an action to the listener — 'how about ~ing?' A gentle recommendation.

spelling.text: 頭が痛いなら、早めに病院に行ったらどうですか。

definition: If you have a headache, why don't you go to the hospital soon?

spelling.text: 疲れているなら、少し休んだらどうですか。

definition: If you're tired, why don't you rest a bit?

spelling.text: 〜たらいいです

patterns.title: 〜tara ii desu — giving light advice or asking what to do
definition: 'It would be good if you ~' — light advice; in a question it asks 'what should I do?'

spelling.text: 疲れたら、少し休んだらいいですよ。

definition: If you're tired, it'd be good to rest a little.

spelling.text: 〜てもらいたい・〜ていただきたい・〜てほしい
〜てほしい / 〜てもらいたい
〜てほしい
〜てもらいたい
〜ていただきたい

patterns.title: Want another person to act / Receive an action / Deferential receiving
definition: Desire: Vて-form + ほしい directly expresses wanting another person to do something. The person can be marked with に. てほしい is not inherently casual; forms such as てほしいです can be polite.
Receiving perspective: Vて-form + もらいたい frames the desired action as something received by the speaker or beneficiary. It is not automatically more polite than てほしい.
Deferential receiving: Vて-form + いただきたい uses the humble receiving verb いただく and shows deference toward the person performing the action.

These constructions are not a fixed three-step politeness scale. Sentence endings, context, the imposition, and the relationship affect the tone; even ていただきたい can sound demanding. A question such as てもらえますか may be more natural for an actual request.

spelling.text: もう少し声を大きくしてほしいんだけど。

definition: I'd like you to speak a little louder.

spelling.text: もっと日本語を勉強してほしいです。

definition: I want you to study Japanese more.

spelling.text: 手伝ってほしいです。

definition: I want you to help me.

spelling.text: 手伝ってもらいたいです。

definition: I'd like to receive your help.

spelling.text: 手伝っていただきたいです。

definition: I'd like to have your assistance.

spelling.text: 手伝ってもらえますか。

definition: Could you help me?

spelling.text: 〜ていただけませんか

patterns.title: 〜te itadakemasen ka — a very polite, humble request
definition: A humble, very polite way to ask someone to do something — the most deferential of the everyday request forms.

spelling.text: すみません、ちょっと手伝っていただけませんか。

definition: Excuse me, could you possibly help me a little?

spelling.text: 〜てくださいませんか

patterns.title: 〜te kudasaimasen ka — a polite negative-form request
definition: A more polite version of 〜てください — uses the honorific くださる in the negative question to soften the request.

spelling.text: すみませんが、窓を開けてくださいませんか。

definition: Excuse me, would you mind opening the window?

spelling.text: 〜てくれませんか

patterns.title: 〜te kuremasen ka — a friendly, informal-polite request
definition: A soft request to a friend or equal — 'won't you do ~ for me?' Uses くれる in the negative question.

spelling.text: ちょっとペンを貸してくれませんか。

definition: Could you lend me a pen for a sec?

spelling.text: 〜といいです

patterns.title: 〜to ii desu — 'I hope ~' / a gentle wish
definition: 'I hope that ~' — expresses a wish that something turns out well, for oneself or another.

spelling.text: 明日、晴れるといいですね。

definition: I hope it's sunny tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜と伝えていただけませんか

patterns.title: 〜to tsutaete itadakemasen ka — politely asking to pass on a message
definition: A polite request asking someone to relay a message to a third party. Quotative と + 伝える + ていただけませんか.

spelling.text: 田中さんに、後で電話すると伝えていただけませんか。

definition: Could you please tell Tanaka-san that I'll call later?

spelling.text: 〜ができます（完成・出現）

patterns.title: 〜ができます (be completed / come into being)
definition: The non-volitional use of できる, meaning something gets finished, comes ready, or newly appears.

spelling.text: ごはんができましたよ。早く来てください。

definition: Uses できました to say the meal is ready.

spelling.text: 〜が聞こえます

patterns.title: 〜が聞こえます (can be heard / is audible)
definition: Expresses that a sound naturally reaches one's ears without trying to listen — spontaneous perception; the thing heard is the subject and takes が.

spelling.text: となりのへやからピアノの音が聞こえます。

definition: Uses が聞こえます for a sound that naturally reaches the ears.

spelling.text: 〜が見えます

patterns.title: 〜が見えます (can be seen / is visible)
definition: Expresses that something naturally enters one's sight without trying to look — spontaneous perception; the thing seen is the subject and takes が.

spelling.text: わたしのへやから海が見えます。

definition: Uses が見えます for scenery that naturally enters view.

spelling.text: 〜が見られる / 〜が聞ける

patterns.title: 〜が見られる / 〜が聞ける (get the chance to see/hear)
definition: The potential form expressing that one can deliberately see or listen because the opportunity exists — different from spontaneous 見える/聞こえる.

spelling.text: この映画館で古い日本の映画が見られます。

definition: Expresses being able to deliberately watch thanks to the opportunity.

spelling.text: 意志動詞・無意志動詞

patterns.title: Volitional vs non-volitional verbs
definition: Volitional verbs express actions a person does on purpose; non-volitional verbs express events or perceptions one cannot control, such as 見える, 聞こえる, できる and 分かる.

spelling.text: ここから富士山が見えます。

definition: 見える is non-volitional, expressing that something naturally comes into view.

spelling.text: V可能形

patterns.title: Verb potential form (how to conjugate)
definition: The single-word verb form meaning 'can do', built by changing the verb ending according to its group.

spelling.text: わたしはひらがなが書けます。

definition: Example of 書ける, the potential of the Group I verb 書く.

spelling.text: 〜ことができる

patterns.title: Can do / Be able to do
definition: Expresses the ability or possibility to do something.
Attaches to a verb's dictionary form to express ability or possibility — the same meaning as the potential form, but slightly more formal.

spelling.text: 彼女はピアノを弾くことができる。

definition: She can play the piano.

spelling.text: ここでカードを使うことができます。

definition: Possibility expressed with the dictionary form 使う + ことができる.

spelling.text: Vているのが見える / 聞こえる

patterns.title: 〜ているのが見える / 聞こえる (see/hear that someone is doing)
definition: Uses の to nominalize a whole action-scene, expressing that the entire situation is naturally seen or heard.

spelling.text: 公園で子どもたちが遊んでいるのが見えます。

definition: Perceives a whole action-scene with のが見えます.

spelling.text: 〜(ら)れる（能力可能）

patterns.title: 〜(ら)れる (ability / possibility)
definition: Uses the potential form to say 'can do' — expressing ability or possibility; the object of the action is marked with が.

spelling.text: ミラーさんは漢字が読めます。

definition: Ability sentence marking the object 漢字 with が.

spelling.text: 自動詞 ↔ 他動詞 (cặp)

patterns.title: Intransitive/transitive verb pairs
definition: Distinguishes paired intransitive and transitive verbs with related forms and meanings.

spelling.text: 私がドアを開けます。

definition: The transitive 開ける takes を.

spelling.text: 自動詞 + ている (trạng thái kết quả)

patterns.title: Intransitive verb + teiru (resultant state)
definition: An intransitive verb + 〜ている expresses a state remaining after a change is complete.

spelling.text: 窓が開いています。

definition: As a result of 開く, the window is open.

spelling.text: 〜ことがある
〜ことがある (偶発)
V辞書形／Vない形 + ことがある
Vた形 + ことがある

patterns.title: Sometimes / Have experienced before
definition: Occasional occurrence: V dictionary-form or Vない-form + ことがある describes something that happens sometimes, rather than an unbroken habit.
Past experience: Vた-form + ことがある means having experienced an action at least once. It does not imply regular repetition or a recent event.

spelling.text: この地域では冬に大雪が降ることがある。

definition: In this region, there are times when heavy snow falls in winter.

spelling.text: 私はときどき朝ごはんを食べないことがあります。

definition: Expresses occasionally skipping breakfast.

spelling.text: 日本に行くことがある。

definition: There are times when I go to Japan.

spelling.text: 日本に行ったことがある。

definition: I've been to Japan before.

spelling.text: まだ〜ている

patterns.title: mada 〜te iru (still doing)
definition: Expresses that an action or state is still continuing now.

spelling.text: 弟はまだ寝ています。

definition: Expresses that the brother is still asleep now.

spelling.text: 〜ながら

patterns.title: 〜nagara (doing two things at once)
definition: Expresses that one person does two actions at the same time.

spelling.text: 音楽を聞きながら、勉強します。

definition: Doing listening and studying at the same time.

spelling.text: 〜ないで (V2 mà không V1)

patterns.title: 〜nai de (without doing)
definition: Expresses doing one action while not doing another; 'without doing ~'.

spelling.text: 朝ごはんを食べないで、学校へ行きました。

definition: Went to school without eating breakfast.

spelling.text: 〜たあとで

patterns.title: 〜ta ato de (after doing)
definition: Expresses doing the next action after a first action has finished; emphasizes the later point in time.

spelling.text: 宿題をしたあとで、テレビを見ます。

definition: Watches TV after finishing homework.

spelling.text: 他動詞 + てある

patterns.title: Transitive verb + tearu (intentional prepared state)
definition: Expresses a state that remains because someone did something intentionally for a purpose.

spelling.text: 窓が開けてあります。

definition: Someone opened the window on purpose; it stays open.

spelling.text: 〜てある vs 〜ている (phân biệt)

patterns.title: 〜tearu vs 〜teiru (distinguishing them)
definition: てある shows a state from someone's intentional act; intransitive + ている shows a state that simply exists.

spelling.text: 窓が開けてあります。

definition: てある: someone opened it on purpose.

spelling.text: 〜ている (thói quen)

patterns.title: 〜teiru (habit / repeated action)
definition: Expresses a habitual action repeated daily or regularly.

spelling.text: 毎朝、コーヒーを飲んでいます。

definition: Expresses a repeated morning habit.

spelling.text: 〜てくる・〜ていく
〜てくる / 〜ていく

patterns.title: ~てくる / ~ていく (direction & change over time)
definition: 〜てくる indicates movement/change toward the speaker or from the past to now; 〜ていく indicates movement/change away from the speaker or continuing from now into the future.
Shows the direction of an action or a change that progresses over time. kuru = toward the speaker, iku = away from the speaker.

spelling.text: 友達が走ってきた。

definition: My friend came running (toward me). — Physical direction: toward the speaker.

spelling.text: ちょっとパンを買ってきます。

definition: Means going to buy bread and coming back.

spelling.text: 〜て (cách thức)

patterns.title: 〜te (manner of an action)
definition: The te-form verb describes the manner or way in which the main action is done.

spelling.text: 毎日歩いて学校へ行きます。

definition: 歩いて describes the manner of going.

spelling.text: 〜てみる

patterns.title: Try doing X (to see what happens)
definition: Expresses the speaker's attempt to do something in order to discover the result or experience; a deliberate 'try and see' action.
To do something experimentally to see what happens; the result is not yet known.

spelling.text: この薬を飲んでみたら、すぐに楽になった。

definition: When I tried taking this medicine, I felt better right away.

spelling.text: この服を着てみてもいいですか。

definition: Asking permission to try the clothes on.

spelling.text: 〜ておく

patterns.title: Do in advance / Leave as-is for a reason
definition: Expresses doing something in advance for a future purpose, or leaving a state as-is intentionally.
Expresses (1) doing something in advance as preparation, or (2) leaving something as it is.

spelling.text: 旅行前に、ホテルを予約しておいた。

definition: I reserved a hotel in advance before the trip.

spelling.text: 旅行の前に、切符を買っておきます。

definition: Buying in advance as preparation.

spelling.text: 〜てしまう

patterns.title: 〜teshimau (completion / regret)
definition: Expresses (1) complete finishing of an action, or (2) regret/unintended result.

spelling.text: 宿題を全部やってしまいました。

definition: Completion sense: finished it all.

spelling.text: て形・た形 (cách chia)

patterns.title: Forming the te-form and ta-form
definition: The basic conjugation that changes verbs into the te-form and ta-form by group.

spelling.text: 本を読んで、寝ます。

definition: Example of the te-form sound change of 読む.

spelling.text: 〜とおりだ・〜どおり（に）
〜とおりに
〜とおりだ
〜どおりに
〜どおりだ

patterns.title: Just as stated or shown / According to a plan or expectation
definition: Core meaning: something corresponds to what was stated, shown, expected, or planned.
Clause attachment: a clause can be followed by とおり, as in 言ったとおり or 先生の言うとおり. とおりに describes carrying out an action in that way.
Noun compound: forms such as 予定どおり use the voiced どおり. とおり and どおり cannot be freely exchanged; the attachment determines the natural form.
Predicate use: とおりだ or どおりだ can state that a result matches the reference, as in 予想どおりでした.

spelling.text: 先生に言われたとおりに、毎日練習しました。

definition: I practised every day exactly as the teacher told me.

spelling.text: 先生が言ったとおりに、書いてください。

definition: Asks to write exactly as the teacher said.

spelling.text: 先生が言ったとおりに書きました。

definition: I wrote it just as the teacher said.

spelling.text: 予定どおりに出発しました。

definition: We departed according to schedule.

spelling.text: 結果は予想どおりでした。

definition: The result was exactly as predicted.

spelling.text: 〜場合は

patterns.title: 〜場合は (in the case of)
definition: 〜場合は states a condition, 'in the case that / should it be that…', in a somewhat formal tone. Common in rules, notices and explanatory texts.

spelling.text: 地震の場合は、エレベーターを使わないでください。

definition: A formal conditional notice using noun + の場合.

spelling.text: 〜ば (điều kiện chung)

patterns.title: 〜ば (general / hypothetical condition)
definition: AばB expresses a hypothesis or general truth: if A holds, B follows. It is favoured for proverbs and natural cause-effect relations.

spelling.text: 春になれば、桜が咲きます。

definition: A general condition stating a natural, inevitable relation.

spelling.text: ば形 (cách chia điều kiện)

patterns.title: How to form the 〜ば conditional
definition: The conjugation rules that turn verbs, i-adjectives, na-adjectives and nouns into their conditional 〜ば (and なら) forms.

spelling.text: ボタンを押せば、ドアが開きます。

definition: An example of the verb 〜ば form, 押す → 押せば.

spelling.text: 〜ないと (いけない)

patterns.title: 〜ないと (いけない) (have to / must)
definition: The conditional と with a negative: 〜しないと（いけない/だめだ）means 'I must / have to do it'. In speech the いけない is often dropped, leaving just 〜ないと。

spelling.text: 明日は早く起きないといけません。

definition: 〜ないといけない expressing an obligation.

spelling.text: 〜なら (điều kiện chủ đề)

patterns.title: 〜なら (contextual / topic conditional)
definition: Takes up what the listener said or the situation as a premise — 'if that's the case / speaking of that' — and then gives advice or an opinion about it. Close to 'as for / regarding'.

spelling.text: 日本語を習うなら、この学校がいいですよ。

definition: Typical なら giving advice on a topic the listener raised.

spelling.text: 〜たら (điều kiện cụ thể)

patterns.title: 〜たら (specific condition / after doing)
definition: The most flexible conditional. AたらB covers a one-time, concrete 'once A happens, then B' as well as 'if A'. The main clause freely allows intention, requests and commands.

spelling.text: 家に帰ったら、すぐに電話します。

definition: Temporal たら meaning 'after / once I do X, then'.

spelling.text: 〜と (điều kiện tự động)

patterns.title: 〜と (automatic / inevitable condition)
definition: AとB expresses an automatic, inevitable result: whenever A happens, B inevitably follows. The main clause cannot contain intention, requests, commands or permission.

spelling.text: このボタンを押すと、切符が出ます。

definition: と showing the inevitable result of operating a machine.

spelling.text: V意向形 (Let's ~)

patterns.title: Volitional form (Let's ~)
definition: Uses '~you' to express one's own will or to casually invite a close person to do something together.

spelling.text: 明日、いっしょに映画を見よう。

definition: A casual invitation to a friend to watch a film together.

spelling.text: V意向形 (cách chia)

patterns.title: Volitional form (verb conjugation)
definition: The plain volitional form '~you / ~ou', conjugated differently by verb group.

spelling.text: 「行く」は「行こう」になります。

definition: Example of a Group 1 verb taking the volitional ending.

spelling.text: 〜ことになる・〜ことになっている
〜ことになる
〜ことになった
〜ことになっている

patterns.title: Settled decision or outcome / Established arrangement / Logical consequence
definition: Decision or outcome: 〜ことになる presents something as settled through circumstances, agreement, or a process, without emphasizing the speaker’s personal agency. It does not necessarily mean the speaker had no influence. 〜ことになった describes the arrangement coming about.
Established arrangement: 〜ことになっている describes an arrangement or rule currently in effect.
Logical consequence: 〜ことになる can state what follows from facts or circumstances, without implying that anyone made a decision.

spelling.text: 来月から東京本社に転勤することになりました。

definition: It has been decided (by the company) that I will transfer to the Tokyo head office starting next month.

spelling.text: 来月、東京へ転勤することになりました。

definition: It was decided (by the company) that I'll transfer to Tokyo next month.

spelling.text: 来月、東京に行くことになりました。

definition: It's been decided that I'll go to Tokyo next month.

spelling.text: 毎週月曜日に会議をすることになっています。

definition: It's established that we have a meeting every Monday.

spelling.text: つまり、全部で三万円かかることになります。

definition: So that means it'll cost 30,000 yen altogether.

spelling.text: 〜ことにする・〜ことにしている
〜ことにする
〜ことにした
〜ことにしている

patterns.title: Make a decision / Maintain a personal rule
definition: Decision: V dictionary-form or Vない-form + ことにする expresses deliberately deciding what one will do or not do. 〜ことにした presents the decision as having been made.
Personal rule: 〜ことにしている describes a policy or rule one has adopted and maintains. It does not guarantee that the person always succeeds in following it.
Contrast with 〜ようにしている: ことにしている emphasizes the adopted decision or personal policy; ようにしている emphasizes continuing effort to put the behavior into practice.

spelling.text: 健康のために、毎日野菜を食べることにした。

definition: I decided to eat vegetables every day for my health.

spelling.text: 来年から大学院に行くことにしました。

definition: I decided by myself to go to graduate school from next year.

spelling.text: 毎朝、歩くことにしました。

definition: I decided to walk every morning.

spelling.text: 毎朝、歩くことにしています。

definition: I've made it my rule to walk every morning.

spelling.text: 〜になる (trở thành / được quyết định)

patterns.title: ~ni naru (become / turn out to be)
definition: Expresses a change of state or an outcome decided naturally or externally.

spelling.text: 弟は来年、大学生になります。

definition: My brother will become a university student next year.

spelling.text: 〜にする (chọn / quyết định)

patterns.title: ~ni suru (choose / decide on)
definition: Expresses choosing or deciding on N from among options.

spelling.text: 私はコーヒーにします。

definition: Choosing coffee when ordering.

spelling.text: 〜予定

patterns.title: ~yotei (be scheduled to ~)
definition: Expresses an objective, already-arranged schedule or plan.

spelling.text: 会議は三時に始まる予定です。

definition: The meeting is scheduled to start at three.

spelling.text: 〜（よ）うと思う
〜(よ)うと思う

patterns.title: Intend to / Plan to
definition: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan to perform an action.
Volitional form + to omou expresses one's intention or decision at the moment of speaking.

spelling.text: 来年の春、大学院に進学しようと思っています。

definition: I am thinking of going on to graduate school next spring.

spelling.text: 夏休みに国へ帰ろうと思います。

definition: An intention to return to one's country during summer break, decided now.

spelling.text: 〜ほうがいい

patterns.title: ~hou ga ii (had better)
definition: 〜したほうがいい / 〜しないほうがいい gives strong advice: 'you'd better (not) do ~'.

spelling.text: 熱があるなら、病院に行ったほうがいいですよ。

definition: 'If you have a fever, you'd better go to the hospital.'

spelling.text: 禁止形 〜な

patterns.title: Prohibitive form '~na'
definition: Dictionary form + な expresses a strong prohibition 'Don't ~!'. As blunt as the imperative.

spelling.text: ここでたばこを吸うな。

definition: A blunt prohibition: 'Don't smoke here!'

spelling.text: 命令形 (cách chia & dùng)

patterns.title: Imperative form (conjugation and use)
definition: A strong, blunt command form like 行け / 食べろ, used for orders, signs, sports cheers and quoted commands. Rough register.

spelling.text: 早く起きろ。

definition: A blunt command: 'Get up quickly!'

spelling.text: 〜なければならない

patterns.title: ~nakereba naranai (must)
definition: From the negative conditional, 〜なければならない / いけない expresses obligation: 'must ~ / have to ~'.

spelling.text: 明日までにこの仕事を終えなければなりません。

definition: 'I must finish this work by tomorrow.'

spelling.text: 〜なくなりました (mất khả năng)

patterns.title: ~naku narimashita (no longer)
definition: Change the negative to 〜なく and add なる to show a change: 'came to no longer ~'. On the potential form it shows loss of ability ('can no longer ~').

spelling.text: 目が悪くなって、小さい字が読めなくなりました。

definition: 'My eyes got worse, so I can no longer read small print.'

spelling.text: 〜なきゃ / 〜なくちゃ

patterns.title: ~nakya / ~nakucha (casual must)
definition: Casual contractions: 〜なければ→〜なきゃ, 〜なくては→〜なくちゃ. They express obligation, 'gotta ~'.

spelling.text: あ、もう行かなきゃ。

definition: 'Oh, I gotta go now.'

spelling.text: 〜なさい

patterns.title: ~nasai (soft command)
definition: Verb ます-stem + なさい: a softer command than the imperative, but still used downward — by parents to children, teachers to students, and in test instructions.

spelling.text: 早く寝なさい。

definition: A parent to a child: 'Go to bed early.'

spelling.text: お〜ください

patterns.title: o~kudasai (honorific request)
definition: お + verb ます-stem + ください is an honorific request meaning 'please ~', elevating the listener. Common in service and announcements.

spelling.text: こちらで少々お待ちください。

definition: 'Please wait here for a moment.'

spelling.text: どういう意味ですか / どういうN

patterns.title: dou iu imi desu ka / dou iu N (what does it mean / what kind of N)
definition: どういう means “what kind of / what sort of.” Used as どういう意味ですか (what does it mean?) and どういうN (what kind of N?).

spelling.text: この言葉はどういう意味ですか。

definition: What does this word mean?

spelling.text: 疑問詞 + か（埋め込み疑問文）

patterns.title: Question word + ka (embedded question)
definition: Embeds a question containing a question word (who/where/when/what/how much) into a larger sentence as plain-form clause + か. The embedded clause stays plain; politeness is carried by the main verb.

spelling.text: パーティーにだれが来るか知っていますか。

definition: Do you know who is coming to the party?

spelling.text: 〜かどうか

patterns.title: Whether or not…
definition: Embeds a yes/no question as a noun clause: 'whether or not…'; the colloquial equivalent of「〜か否か」.
Used to embed a yes/no question (no question word) as plain form + かどうか, meaning “whether (or not).” The embedded part is plain form.

spelling.text: 彼が来るかどうか、まだわからない。

definition: I still don't know whether or not he will come.

spelling.text: 彼が来るかどうか分かりません。

definition: I don't know whether he will come or not.

spelling.text: 〜のを知っていますか

patterns.title: 〜no o shitte imasu ka (do you know that ~?)
definition: Asks whether the listener knows a certain fact/event. The clause is nominalized with plain form + の (こと), followed by を知っていますか.

spelling.text: 田中さんが結婚したのを知っていますか。

definition: Do you know that Tanaka got married?

spelling.text: 〜のを忘れました

patterns.title: 〜no o wasuremashita (forgot to ~)
definition: Expresses forgetting to do an action one intended to do. Verb dictionary form + のを忘れました; の nominalizes the verb phrase as the object of 忘れる.

spelling.text: 薬を飲むのを忘れました。

definition: I forgot to take my medicine.

spelling.text: 〜と言っていました

patterns.title: 〜to itte imashita (reporting someone's words)
definition: Used to report to someone what another person said. The quoted content takes the plain form before と.

spelling.text: 田中さんは明日休むと言っていました。

definition: Tanaka said (he/she) will take tomorrow off.

spelling.text: 〜という意味です

patterns.title: 〜to iu imi desu (it means ~)
definition: Used to explain the meaning of a word or expression. The word/clause being explained (plain form) goes before という.

spelling.text: 「立入禁止」は入ってはいけないという意味です。

definition: “Tachiiri kinshi” means you must not enter.

spelling.text: 〜というN / っていうN

patterns.title: 〜to iu N / 〜tte iu N (an N called ~)
definition: Introduces or specifies a noun by its name. 〜という + noun means “an N named/called ~.” Casual: っていう.

spelling.text: 田中さんという人から電話がありました。

definition: There was a call from a person named Tanaka.

spelling.text: 〜と / って言う

patterns.title: 〜to / tte iu (quotation)
definition: Quotes what someone says or thinks. Direct quotation: 「…」と言う; indirect: plain-form clause + と言う. In speech と becomes って.

spelling.text: 彼は「また来ます」と言いました。

definition: He said, “I'll come again.”

spelling.text: 〜と読みます / 〜と書いてあります

patterns.title: 〜to yomimasu / 〜to kaite arimasu (read as / written as)
definition: Marks how a character is read, or what is written on a paper/sign. The reading or text is quoted directly with と.

spelling.text: この漢字は「みず」と読みます。

definition: This kanji is read “mizu.”

spelling.text: 〜でしょう / 〜だろう

patterns.title: 〜deshou / 〜darou (probably / I suppose)
definition: Expresses the speaker's conjecture ('probably... / I suppose...'), said with a falling intonation. でしょう is polite, だろう is plain. Medium certainty; usable even without explicit evidence.

spelling.text: 明日はたぶん晴れるでしょう。

definition: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜がる / 〜がっている

patterns.title: 〜garu / 〜gatte iru (showing a third person's feeling)
definition: Attaching がる to emotion/sensation adjectives (ほしい, こわい, うれしい…) objectively describes a third person outwardly showing that feeling. Ongoing/current state uses がっている.

spelling.text: 子どもが新しいおもちゃをほしがっている。

definition: The child wants the new toy.

spelling.text: 〜がする

patterns.title: 〜ga suru (there is a sound/smell/taste/feeling)
definition: Expresses a perception felt through the senses or body—sound, smell, taste, chill, feeling—using 〜がする. Characteristically used for senses other than sight.

spelling.text: 台所からいいにおいがする。

definition: There's a nice smell coming from the kitchen.

spelling.text: 〜はずがない

patterns.title: Cannot possibly be so / Contrary to reasoned expectation
definition: 〜はずがない strongly rejects a possibility because it conflicts with what the speaker knows or expects: “that cannot fit the facts or my understanding.”
Contrast with 〜わけがない: the latter can sound more categorical or emotional. This is a tendency rather than a fixed rule; the expressions overlap, and context and tone can matter more than the choice.

spelling.text: 彼がそんな嘘をつくはずがない。ずっと正直な人だったのに。

definition: There's no way he would tell such a lie. He has always been an honest person.

spelling.text: あんなにまじめな彼が、うそをつくはずがない。

definition: Someone as honest as him can't possibly be lying.

spelling.text: 彼がそんなことをするはずがない。

definition: He couldn't possibly do something like that.

spelling.text: 〜わけがない

patterns.title: There's no way / Categorical rejection
definition: 〜わけがない rejects a possibility categorically, often with a stronger or more emotional tone: it makes no sense or there is no way it could happen.

Contrast with 〜はずがない: はずがない presents disbelief as conflicting with known facts or expectations. This distinction is a tendency rather than an absolute rule; both expressions can fit many of the same situations.

spelling.text: 彼がそんなことをするわけがない。

definition: There's no way he'd do something like that.

spelling.text: 〜はずだ
〜はず

patterns.title: Should be / Ought to be (reasoned expectation)
definition: Expresses a confident expectation or deduction based on known information; 'should be', 'ought to be'.

Expresses a logical expectation: based on solid evidence (a fact, knowledge, or a promise), the speaker concludes that something should/ought to be the case. It signals confident inference, not mere hope.

spelling.text: 彼女は毎日練習しているから、もう上手なはずだ。

definition: She practices every day, so she should be good by now.

spelling.text: 彼は今日休みだから、家にいるはずです。

definition: He's off today, so he should be at home.

spelling.text: 〜かもしれない

patterns.title: 〜kamoshirenai (might / may / perhaps)
definition: Expresses a possibility ('it might be the case that...'). Lower certainty than でしょう/だろう, acknowledging that it may or may not be true.

spelling.text: 空が暗いから、もしかしたら雨が降るかもしれない。

definition: The sky is dark, so it might rain.

spelling.text: 〜みたいだ

patterns.title: 〜mitai da (it seems / looks like — casual)
definition: The casual, colloquial counterpart of ようだ. Used to make a subjective inference from what you've seen/heard, or to liken something to something else. Common in conversation.

spelling.text: 外は寒いみたいだ。みんなコートを着ている。

definition: It looks cold outside—everyone's wearing coats.

spelling.text: 〜らしい

patterns.title: Seems like / Apparently
definition: Expresses conjecture or hearsay based on information or evidence the speaker has received.

Expresses an inference based on information from outside (what others say, rumor, news): 'apparently...'. The speaker is not directly involved and places the basis of the claim with that outside source.

spelling.text: 彼はもう会社を辞めたらしい。

definition: It seems he has already quit the company.

spelling.text: 天気予報によると、明日は雨らしい。

definition: According to the forecast, it's apparently going to rain tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜そうだ（様態）

patterns.title: 〜sou da (looks like / seems — by appearance)
definition: Based on the appearance in front of you, expresses an intuitive judgment ('it looks like... / it's about to...'). Describes a sign before something happens or an impression purely from looking.

spelling.text: 空が暗くなってきた。今にも雨が降りそうだ。

definition: The sky has darkened—it looks like it's about to rain.

spelling.text: 〜そうだ（伝聞）

patterns.title: 〜sou da (I hear that / they say — hearsay)
definition: Reports information you heard from someone or learned from a book/news, conveying it as-is ('I hear that...'). The speaker adds no judgment, objectively relaying the source's content.

spelling.text: ニュースによると、来週から寒くなるそうだ。

definition: According to the news, it's going to get cold from next week.

spelling.text: 〜たがる / 〜たがっている

patterns.title: 〜tagaru / 〜tagatte iru (a third person wants to do)
definition: Formed by adding がる to the desire form 〜たい; objectively describes a third person outwardly showing the wish to do something. Current state uses たがっている.

spelling.text: 弟は新しいゲームをやりたがっている。

definition: My little brother wants to play the new game.

spelling.text: 〜ようだ

patterns.title: 〜you da (it seems / it appears)
definition: Based on what the speaker has personally seen, heard, or felt, expresses a subjective inference ('it seems that...'). A fairly confident judgment grounded in direct evidence.

spelling.text: 道がぬれている。夜の間に雨が降ったようだ。

definition: The road is wet—it seems it rained during the night.

spelling.text: 直接受身 (N1はN2に〜られる)

patterns.title: Direct passive (N1 is V-ed by N2)
definition: A passive where the subject is the direct recipient of the action; the agent is marked with に.

spelling.text: 私は先生にほめられました。

definition: I was praised by the teacher.

spelling.text: 客観受身 (Nは/が〜られる)

patterns.title: Objective passive (N is V-ed)
definition: A passive that takes a thing as subject without stating the agent; used in objective writing such as news and notices.

spelling.text: このお寺は400年前に建てられました。

definition: This temple was built 400 years ago.

spelling.text: 迷惑・所有物受身 (N3を〜られる)

patterns.title: Adversative / possessive passive (had N3 V-ed on me)
definition: A passive expressing that the subject is inconvenienced or harmed by another's action; a possession or body part stays marked with を.

spelling.text: 電車の中で足を踏まれました。

definition: My foot got stepped on in the train.

spelling.text: 〜によって (tác nhân bị động)

patterns.title: ~によって (agent marker in passive)
definition: In passives of invention, discovery, or creation, ~によって marks the agent who performed the act.

spelling.text: 電話はベルによって発明されました。

definition: The telephone was invented by Bell.

spelling.text: 〜(さ)せられる (使役受身)

patterns.title: ~(sa)serareru (causative-passive: be made to do)
definition: Expresses being forced by someone to do an action unwillingly; conveys the reluctant nuance of 'was made to do'.

spelling.text: 私は母に毎日部屋を片付けさせられました。

definition: I was made by my mother to tidy my room every day.

spelling.text: 〜(さ)せる (使役)

patterns.title: ~(sa)seru (causative: make / let someone do)
definition: Expresses making someone do an action (compulsion) or letting them do it (permission).

spelling.text: 母は子供を公園で遊ばせました。

definition: The mother let her child play in the park.

spelling.text: 〜させていただけませんか

patterns.title: ~させていただけませんか (may I be allowed to do?)
definition: Causative + humble + question; the most polite way to ask 'may I be allowed to do ~?'.

spelling.text: 来週、お休みを取らせていただけませんか。

definition: Might I be allowed to take leave next week?

spelling.text: 〜させてください

patterns.title: Please allow me to ~
definition: A polite expression in which the speaker humbly requests permission from the listener to perform an action.
Causative form + てください; politely asks for permission to do something oneself.

spelling.text: 少し休憩させてください。

definition: Please allow me to take a short rest.

spelling.text: その仕事は私にやらせてください。

definition: Please let me do that job.

spelling.text: 使役形 (cách chia)

patterns.title: Causative form conjugation (3 verb groups)
definition: The conjugation rules for changing a verb into its causative form (~(sa)seru); the method differs by verb group.

spelling.text: 先生は学生を立たせます。

definition: stand → make stand (Group I)

spelling.text: 使役受身形 (cách chia)

patterns.title: Causative-passive form conjugation (3 verb groups)
definition: The conjugation rules for the causative-passive form (~(sa)serareru); Group I also has a contracted form.

spelling.text: 子供のとき、毎日ピアノを練習させられました。

definition: practice → be made to practice (suru type)

spelling.text: ていねい形 vs ふつう形

patterns.title: Polite form vs plain form
definition: The stylistic distinction between polite form (です・ます) and plain form (dictionary form・だ), chosen by relationship and situation.

spelling.text: （先生に）明日はテストがありますか。

definition: (To a teacher) Is there a test tomorrow?

spelling.text: 受身形 (cách chia)

patterns.title: Passive form conjugation (3 verb groups)
definition: The conjugation rules for changing a verb into its passive form (~rareru); the method differs by verb group.

spelling.text: 先生は学生をほめます。→ 学生は先生にほめられます。

definition: praise → be praised (Group II)

spelling.text: Nに Nを あげる / さしあげる / やる

patterns.title: あげる / さしあげる / やる (to give)
definition: Expresses the speaker (or someone in the speaker's in-group) giving something to another person. The verb level matches the recipient's status: さしあげる for superiors, あげる for equals, やる for inferiors/animals/plants. The recipient is marked by に.

spelling.text: わたしは友だちにプレゼントをあげました。

definition: I gave my friend a present.

spelling.text: Nが（私に）Nを くれる / くださる

patterns.title: くれる / くださる (someone gives to me)
definition: Expresses another person giving something to the speaker or the speaker's in-group. The recipient is always わたし or someone on the speaker's side. If the giver is a superior, the honorific くださる is used.

spelling.text: 友だちがわたしに花をくれました。

definition: My friend gave me flowers.

spelling.text: Nは Nに/から Nを もらう / いただく

patterns.title: もらう / いただく (to receive)
definition: Expresses the speaker or the speaker's in-group receiving something from another person. The viewpoint is on the receiver. The giver is marked by に or から, and いただく (humble) is used when the giver is a superior.

spelling.text: わたしは友だちにチョコレートをもらいました。

definition: I received chocolate from my friend.

spelling.text: Vて あげる / さしあげる / やる

patterns.title: 〜てあげる (do something for someone)
definition: Expresses the speaker or speaker's in-group performing an action as a favor for another person. The focus is on giving a benefit through an action rather than handing over an object. Choose さしあげる / あげる / やる by the recipient's status.

spelling.text: わたしは友だちに本を貸してあげました。

definition: I lent my friend a book (as a favor).

spelling.text: 〜てくださる / 〜ていただく

patterns.title: 〜てくださる / 〜ていただく (honorific giving & receiving)
definition: When a superior does an action for the speaker's side: use the honorific 〜てくださる if the viewpoint is on the doer, and the humble 〜ていただく if the viewpoint is on the beneficiary. They describe the same scene from two viewpoints.

spelling.text: 先生が推薦状を書いてくださいました。

definition: My teacher wrote me a letter of recommendation (honorific).

spelling.text: Vて くれる / くださる

patterns.title: 〜てくれる (someone does something for me)
definition: Expresses another person doing an action as a favor for the speaker or speaker's in-group. The beneficiary is always the speaker's side. If the doer is a superior, use the honorific 〜てくださる.

spelling.text: 友だちが宿題を手伝ってくれました。

definition: My friend helped me with my homework.

spelling.text: Nに Vて もらう / いただく

patterns.title: 〜てもらう (have / get someone to do something)
definition: Expresses the speaker or speaker's in-group having another person do an action and receiving its benefit. The viewpoint is on the beneficiary. The doer is marked by に, and 〜ていただく (humble) is used when the doer is a superior.

spelling.text: わたしは友だちに引っ越しを手伝ってもらいました。

definition: I had my friend help me with the move.

spelling.text: Vて さしあげる

patterns.title: 〜てさしあげる (humble: do something for a superior)
definition: A humble expression for the speaker or speaker's in-group doing an action for a social superior. It is the humble counterpart of 〜てあげる.

spelling.text: わたしは部長を駅まで送ってさしあげました。

definition: I saw the department head off to the station (humble).

spelling.text: N／疑問詞 ＋ でも

patterns.title: 〜でも (even ~; any ~ at all)
definition: Attached to a noun, it raises an extreme example to imply 'even this case applies'. Attached to a question word it gives a sweeping 'any-/every-' meaning.

spelling.text: そんなことは子どもでも知っています。

definition: Even a child knows something like that.

spelling.text: 普通形／丁寧形 ＋ から

patterns.title: 〜から (because; subjective reason)
definition: Gives a subjective reason based on the speaker's judgment. It works well with clauses expressing the speaker's will, commands, invitations, or guesses.

spelling.text: もう遅いから、そろそろ帰りましょう。

definition: It's late, so let's head home soon.

spelling.text: 〜のに
普通形（なAdjは〜な／Nは〜な） + のに

patterns.title: Even though ~ / and yet ~
definition: A contrastive conjunction expressing that despite the fact in the first clause, the outcome in the second clause is contrary to the speaker's expectation, conveying disappointment, dissatisfaction, or surprise.

A contrastive expression where the result that follows is unexpected and contrary to what the first clause would lead you to expect, as in 'Even though I studied a lot, I failed the exam.' It often carries the speaker's surprise, regret, or reproach.

spelling.text: あんなに練習したのに、試験に落ちてしまった。

definition: Even though I practiced so much, I ended up failing the exam.

spelling.text: たくさん勉強したのに、試験に落ちてしまいました。

definition: Even though I studied a lot, I ended up failing the exam.

spelling.text: V辞書形 + のに（＋使う・要る・便利だ等）

patterns.title: 〜のに (for the purpose of / used for)
definition: Vのに expresses a purpose or use: 'for doing ~' / 'used for ~.' The following clause states an evaluation, cost, or time related to that use, with words like 使う, 要る, 必要だ, 便利だ, or かかる. It is distinct from the contrastive のに and attaches only to a verb in dictionary form.

spelling.text: このはさみは紙を切るのに使います。

definition: These scissors are used for cutting paper.

spelling.text: 普通形 ＋ し、〜し

patterns.title: 〜し (and what's more; listing reasons)
definition: Lists two or more reasons or facts, stacking them up as '〜し、〜し'. It often implies an unstated 'and so…' conclusion.

spelling.text: この店は安いし、おいしいし、よく来ます。

definition: This place is cheap and tasty, so I come often.

patterns.title: それで (and so; therefore)
definition: A conjunction that takes the previous sentence as a cause/reason and states the resulting outcome in the next. Softer than だから, it suits narrating a chain of events that already happened.

spelling.text: きのうは熱がありました。それで、会社を休みました。

definition: I had a fever yesterday. And so, I took the day off work.

spelling.text: 普通形（NはNの／なAdjは〜な） + ため（に）

patterns.title: 〜ため(に) (because of / due to)
definition: A somewhat formal way of stating the cause or reason for something; the result usually follows, as in 'Because of an accident, the train was delayed.' It sounds more formal than ので/から for giving reasons and is common in written notices and news.

spelling.text: 事故のため、電車が三十分遅れました。

definition: The train was 30 minutes late because of an accident.

spelling.text: V辞書形 / Nの + ために

patterns.title: 〜ために (in order to / for the purpose of)
definition: Expresses doing a deliberate action in order to achieve a goal. Both clauses share the same subject, and the front clause uses a volitional verb in dictionary form, or a noun + の. The purpose comes first and the action taken to realise it comes second, as in 'I came to Japan in order to study Japanese.'

spelling.text: 日本語を勉強するために日本へ来ました。

definition: I came to Japan in order to study Japanese.

spelling.text: Vて／Aくて／Aで／Nで（原因・理由）

patterns.title: 〜て / 〜で (cause; natural result)
definition: Shows that the first event is the cause or trigger and the second naturally follows. The result clause is non-volitional — feelings, states, or spontaneous outcomes.

spelling.text: 急いでいて、財布を忘れました。

definition: I was in a hurry, so I forgot my wallet.

spelling.text: Vても／Aくても／なAでも／Nでも

patterns.title: 〜ても (even if; even though)
definition: A concessive conditional: even if the stated condition holds, the result contrary to expectation does not change. Roughly 'even if ~'.

spelling.text: 雨が降っても、試合は行います。

definition: Even if it rains, the match will be held.

spelling.text: V辞書形／Vない形 + ように + 言う／伝える／注意する／頼む

patterns.title: 〜ように言う / 注意する (to tell/instruct someone to ~)
definition: A way of reporting that you indirectly instructed, asked, or warned someone to do (or not do) something. The content of the command or request is wrapped in 〜ように and joined to verbs like 言う, 伝える, 頼む, or 注意する. It summarises the content rather than quoting directly.

spelling.text: 先生は学生に毎日漢字を練習するように言いました。

definition: The teacher told the students to practise kanji every day.

spelling.text: 〜ようになる
V辞書形／V可能形／Vない形 + ようになる

patterns.title: Come to be able to / Come to do
definition: Expresses a gradual or natural change in state, habit, or ability from what it was before.

Expresses the result of a change: something one could not do, or did not do, comes to be possible or habitual. Often a potential form + ようになる, as in 'I came to be able to ~,' describing a change in ability or habit. For a negative change, use 〜なくなる.

spelling.text: 毎日練習したら、漢字が書けるようになりました。

definition: As a result of practicing every day, I came to be able to write kanji.

spelling.text: 練習して、自転車に乗れるようになりました。

definition: After practising, I became able to ride a bicycle.

spelling.text: 〜ように（目的）
V辞書形／Vない形 + ように

patterns.title: 〜ように — in order to / so that (purpose)
definition: Expresses purpose or desired result (so that, in order to); the preceding verb is typically in the potential or negative form, and the main clause shows the speaker's effort or action.

Expresses acting so that a desired state comes about. The preceding verb is typically a potential, a non-volitional verb, or a negative (e.g. 読める, 忘れない), and the subject may differ between clauses. Whereas ために states a deliberate aim, ように expresses a result-oriented purpose: 'so that it turns out this way.'

spelling.text: 日本語が話せるように、毎日練習しています。

definition: I practise every day so that I can speak Japanese. (purpose of achieving ability)

spelling.text: 後ろの席の人にも聞こえるように、大きい声で話しました。

definition: I spoke loudly so that the people in the back seats could also hear.

spelling.text: V辞書形／Vない形 + ようにしてください

patterns.title: 〜ようにしてください (please make sure to / try to)
definition: A polite request asking the listener to make a continuous effort to do something. Softer than the direct 〜てください, it urges effort or care. The negative 〜ないようにしてください means 'please try not to do ~.'

spelling.text: 毎日薬を飲むようにしてください。

definition: Please make sure to take your medicine every day.

spelling.text: 〜ようにする・〜ようにしている
V辞書形／Vない形 + ようにする
〜ようにしている

patterns.title: Make an effort / Maintain a continuing effort
definition: New effort: V dictionary-form or Vない-form + ようにする expresses conscious effort to bring about an action or state, or to avoid one. 〜ないようにする means making an effort not to do something.
Continuing effort: 〜ようにしている describes trying to maintain a practice or making a point of doing something regularly.
Contrast with 〜ことにしている: ようにしている emphasizes continuing effort; ことにしている emphasizes an adopted decision or personal policy. Both can describe the same behavior from different perspectives.

spelling.text: 健康のために、毎日30分は歩くようにしている。

definition: For my health, I make a point of walking for 30 minutes every day.

spelling.text: 健康のために、毎日野菜を食べるようにしています。

definition: For my health, I make a point of eating vegetables every day.

spelling.text: 毎朝、歩くようにします。

definition: I'll make an effort to walk every morning.

spelling.text: 毎朝、歩くようにしています。

definition: I try to make a point of walking every morning.

spelling.text: V[ます-stem] + 始める / 出す

patterns.title: 〜始める / 〜出す (start doing)
definition: Compound verbs marking the start of an action or change. 〜始める typically implies a deliberate or gradual beginning, while 〜出す often implies a sudden, unexpected onset. Both attach to the ます-stem.

spelling.text: 去年から日本語を習い始めました。

definition: I started learning Japanese last year.

spelling.text: AはBほど〜ない

patterns.title: 〜ほど〜ない (A is not as 〜 as B)
definition: A negative comparison stating that topic A does not reach the degree of standard B. The predicate is always negative. It can also be phrased BほどAは〜ない.

spelling.text: 今日は昨日ほど寒くないです。

definition: Today is not as cold as yesterday.

spelling.text: V[ます-stem] + 方（かた）

patterns.title: 〜方 (the way of doing ~)
definition: Attaches 方 (かた) to the ます-stem of a verb to form a noun meaning 'the way of doing / how to do ~'. As in 読み方 (how to read), 使い方 (how to use), 作り方 (how to make), it indicates how the action is performed. The resulting word is a noun taking が, を, は.

spelling.text: この漢字の読み方を教えてください。

definition: Please tell me how to read this kanji.

spelling.text: [普通形] + こと（名詞化）

patterns.title: こと (nominalizer — turning a verb or clause into a noun)
definition: Adds こと after a verb or clause to nominalize it. Used for abstract or general matters, the content of thoughts or reports, and fixed expressions (〜ことができる, 〜ことにする, 趣味は〜こと). It is stiffer than の and suits written or explanatory sentences.

spelling.text: わたしの趣味は写真を撮ることです。

definition: My hobby is taking photos.

spelling.text: V[ます-stem] → N（連用形の名詞用法）

patterns.title: ます-stem used as a noun (帰り, 始まり, etc.)
definition: A usage where the ます-stem (連用形) of a verb is used directly as a noun: 帰ります → 帰り (return), 始まります → 始まり (beginning), 終わります → 終わり (end), 考えます → 考え (thought). It forms nouns for actions or states. Not every verb allows this; many are conventionally fixed words.

spelling.text: 会社の帰りにスーパーで買い物をします。

definition: On the way home from work, I shop at the supermarket.

spelling.text: 〜にくい
V[ます-stem] + にくい

patterns.title: Hard to do / difficult to
definition: Expresses that something is difficult to do or hard to achieve, describing a property or unfavorable condition.
The opposite of 〜やすい: expresses that an action is hard to do, or that something is unlikely to happen. It attaches to the ます-stem and conjugates as an いAdjective.

spelling.text: この漢字は画数が多くて書きにくい。

definition: This kanji has many strokes and is hard to write.

spelling.text: この薬は苦くて飲みにくいです。

definition: This medicine is bitter and hard to take.

spelling.text: [動詞辞書形] + のが + 好き / 上手 / 下手 / 苦手

patterns.title: 〜のが好き / 上手 (の + feeling / ability predicate)
definition: Nominalizes an action with 動詞＋の, then marks it with が to make it the object of a feeling/ability predicate such as 好き, 嫌い, 上手, 下手, 苦手, 速い. (動作)するのが好きだ / 上手だ means 'likes / is good at doing ~'.

spelling.text: 妹は絵をかくのが好きです。

definition: My little sister likes drawing pictures.

spelling.text: [普通形] + の（名詞化）

patterns.title: の (nominalizer — turning a verb or clause into a noun)
definition: Adds の after a verb or clause to treat that action or event as a single noun. The nominalized part can take particles like が, を, は and serve as the subject or object of a sentence. It is especially used with perception (see, hear) and concrete actions.

spelling.text: わたしは音楽を聞くのが好きです。

definition: I like listening to music.

spelling.text: V[ます-stem] + 終わる / 続ける

patterns.title: 〜終わる / 〜続ける (finish doing / keep doing)
definition: Compound verbs marking the phase of an action. 〜終わる means the action is carried through to completion; 〜続ける means the action continues without interruption. Both attach to the ます-stem.

spelling.text: やっとレポートを書き終わりました。

definition: I finally finished writing the report.

spelling.text: い-Adj(語幹) + さ / み ・ な-Adj(語幹) + さ

patterns.title: 〜さ / 〜み (turning an adjective into a noun)
definition: Suffixes that turn an adjective into a noun. さ attaches to the stem to express the objective degree or measurable extent of a quality (length, size, convenience). み attaches to a limited set of adjectives to express, more subjectively, the state or felt quality (heft, warmth, enjoyment).

spelling.text: この橋の長さは２キロメートルあります。

definition: The length of this bridge is two kilometers.

spelling.text: AとBとどちらが〜か

patterns.title: 〜と〜とどちらが〜か (which of A and B is more 〜?)
definition: A comparative question naming two items and asking which ranks higher in some quality. The answer is '(B)のほうが〜'. For three or more items, use どれ / だれ / いつ / どこ instead of どちら.

spelling.text: コーヒーと紅茶と、どちらがいいですか。

definition: Which would you prefer, coffee or tea?

spelling.text: 〜やすい
V[ます-stem] + やすい

patterns.title: Easy to do / prone to
definition: Expresses that something is easy to do or prone to a certain state — usable for ability and tendency.

Expresses that an action is easy to do, or that something readily tends to happen. It attaches to the ます-stem and the whole word conjugates like an いAdjective. It covers both objective properties and subjective ease.

spelling.text: このペンは書きやすいので、いつも使っている。

definition: This pen is easy to write with, so I always use it.

spelling.text: このペンは書きやすいです。

definition: This pen is easy to write with.

spelling.text: AよりBのほうが〜

patterns.title: 〜より〜のほうが (B is more 〜 than A)
definition: Compares two things and states that one ranks higher in some quality. The standard of comparison takes より, and the item said to be greater takes のほうが. The order of the two phrases can be swapped.

spelling.text: 電車より車のほうが速いです。

definition: The car is faster than the train.

spelling.text: 〜間に / 〜とき(に)

patterns.title: 〜間に / 〜とき(に) (while / when)
definition: 「間に」 expresses that another event happens once during a continuing period. 「とき(に)」 marks a point or scene in time, with before/after relation determined by verb form (dictionary = before, ta = after). 「間」 (without に) means something lasts throughout the whole period, distinct from 「間に」.

spelling.text: わたしが寝ている間に、地震がありました。

definition: There was an earthquake while I was asleep.

spelling.text: 〜ばかり / 〜たばかり
