patterns.title: 〜ばかり (only / nothing but; just finished)
definition: 「ばかり」 after a noun or te-form means "nothing but / always doing only that," expressing a one-sided excess. 「たばかり」 after a verb's ta-form means "just finished doing," indicating something happened a moment ago. The latter can be used even after some time if the speaker feels it was recent.

spelling.text: 弟は休みの日にゲームばかりしています。

definition: My brother does nothing but play games on his days off.

spelling.text: 〜だけ
N / V / A ＋ だけ

patterns.title: Only / Just X
definition: Limits scope to X alone, excluding everything else; softer and more neutral than しか〜ない.

だけ marks a neutral limit on a range, quantity, or target, stating matter-of-factly that "there is nothing besides this." Unlike しか〜ない, it carries no sense of insufficiency. It attaches not only to nouns but also to verbs, adjectives, and clauses.

spelling.text: 彼女は野菜だけ食べて、肉は全く食べない。

definition: She eats only vegetables and doesn't eat meat at all.

spelling.text: 朝はコーヒーだけ飲みます。

definition: In the morning I drink only coffee.

spelling.text: 助詞「で」の用法（場所・手段・範囲・原因）

patterns.title: The particle で (place, means, scope, cause)
definition: で has four main uses: (1) place where an action occurs (公園で遊ぶ); (2) means, tool, or material (バスで行く, 木で作る); (3) scope or limit (一日で読む, 三人で行く); (4) cause or reason (病気で休む). Note the difference from に, which marks location of existence.

spelling.text: 図書館で勉強します。

definition: I study at the library.

spelling.text: 副詞（まだ・もう・きっと・ぜひ など）

patterns.title: 副詞 (adverbs of degree, certainty, and desire)
definition: Words that modify verbs, adjectives, or whole sentences. 「まだ・もう」 express the stage of time or state, 「きっと・たぶん」 the degree of certainty, 「ぜひ」 a strong wish or recommendation. A key feature is that many require agreement with the predicate's form (affirmative/negative).

spelling.text: 宿題はまだ終わっていません。

definition: I haven't finished my homework yet.

spelling.text: 敬語入門（尊敬語・謙譲語・丁寧語）

patterns.title: Introduction to keigo (respectful, humble, polite)
definition: Japanese keigo divides into three types. Respectful language (尊敬語) elevates the actions of the listener or a third party to show deference (お〜になる, いらっしゃる); humble language (謙譲語) lowers one's own actions to elevate the other party (お〜する, いたす, 参る); polite language (丁寧語) makes the speech itself courteous with です・ます. The crucial distinction is direction: 尊敬語 for the other's actions, 謙譲語 for one's own.

spelling.text: 先生はもうお帰りになりました。

definition: The teacher has already gone home (respectful).

spelling.text: こそあど（こ・そ・あ・ど系）

patterns.title: こそあど (the ko-so-a-do demonstrative system)
definition: A system of demonstratives where こ = near the speaker, そ = near the listener or something just mentioned, あ = far from both / mutually known, ど = interrogative. Each row pairs across types: thing (これ), adnominal (この), place (ここ), direction (こちら), manner (こんな), and adverb (こう).

spelling.text: これはわたしのかさですが、それはだれのですか。

definition: This is my umbrella, but whose is that one near you?

spelling.text: 〜まで / 〜までに

patterns.title: 〜まで / 〜までに (until / by a deadline)
definition: 「まで」 marks the end point up to which an action or state continues without interruption. 「までに」 marks a deadline by which a single action must be completed. Use 「まで」 with continuous actions and 「までに」 with one-time, completion-type actions.

spelling.text: 3時まで図書館で勉強します。

definition: I study at the library until 3 o'clock.

spelling.text: 〜まま

patterns.title: As is / Leaving the state unchanged
definition: Expresses that an action is performed while a certain state remains unchanged — the state is maintained as-is.

Expresses that another action is done while a certain state remains unchanged. It often implies that a state which would normally be changed is left as it is. Connects to verb ta-form/nai-form, i-adjectives, na-adjective + な, and noun + の.

spelling.text: 靴を履いたまま、部屋に入ってしまった。

definition: I entered the room with my shoes still on (without taking them off).

spelling.text: 窓を開けたまま出かけてしまいました。

definition: I went out with the window left open.

spelling.text: 助詞「も」の用法（同類・累加・数量強調）

patterns.title: The particle も (also, even, emphasizing quantity)
definition: も basically means "also/too" (わたしも行く). At N4 we also organize: (2) quantity + も to express "more than expected," with surprise/emphasis (三時間も待った); and (3) interrogative + も + negative for total negation (だれも来ない, 何もない).

spelling.text: わたしも来月日本へ行きます。

definition: I, too, am going to Japan next month.

spelling.text: 助詞「に」の用法（目的・頻度・割合・対象）

patterns.title: The particle に (purpose, frequency, ratio, target)
definition: Key uses of に that expand at N4 are: (1) purpose of movement (買い物に行く = V-stem + に); (2) basis of frequency (一週間に三回); (3) ratio/distribution (一人に二つ); (4) target or partner of an action (友だちに会う, 先生に聞く). These build on the basic に for existence, time, and destination.

spelling.text: デパートへ服を買いに行きます。

definition: I'm going to the department store to buy clothes.

spelling.text: 助詞「を」の用法（対象・起点・通過・移動）

patterns.title: The particle を (object, departure, passage, motion)
definition: を has four main uses: (1) object of an action (本を読む); (2) point of departure/separation (家を出る, 大学を卒業する); (3) place of passage/motion (道を歩く, 橋を渡る); (4) target of a causative (子どもを行かせる). Uses (2) and (3) combine with intransitive verbs, unlike the object use (1).

spelling.text: 毎晩、日本語の本を読みます。

definition: Every evening I read a Japanese book.

spelling.text: 接続詞（それに・けれど・たとえば など）

patterns.title: 接続詞 (conjunctions linking sentences)
definition: Independent words that show the logical relation between sentences. They are chosen by relation type: addition (それに, しかも), contrast (けれど, しかし, ところが), example (たとえば), choice (または, それとも), topic shift (ところで). Placed at the head of a sentence to link the previous and following ones.

spelling.text: この店は安いです。それに、料理もおいしいです。

definition: This restaurant is cheap. Moreover, the food is delicious too.

spelling.text: N（＋助詞）＋しか ＋ 〜ない

patterns.title: 〜しか〜ない (only; nothing but)
definition: しか always pairs with a negative verb to mark a strong limitation meaning "nothing but / only." It carries the speaker's feeling that the amount or range is small or insufficient. Unlike the neutral だけ, しか〜ない adds a nuance of "that is all there is," often with mild regret.

spelling.text: 財布の中に百円しかありません。

definition: I have only 100 yen in my wallet.

spelling.text: 終助詞（〜ね・〜よ・〜かな など）

patterns.title: 終助詞 (sentence-final particles)
definition: Particles attached at the end of a sentence to convey the speaker's feeling or attitude toward the listener. 「ね」 seeks confirmation or agreement, 「よ」 informs the listener of something they don't know, 「よね」 confirms while seeking agreement, and 「かな(あ)」 expresses a self-directed question or hesitation.

spelling.text: 今日はいい天気ですね。

definition: It's nice weather today, isn't it?

spelling.text: 〜途中で / 〜途中に

patterns.title: 〜途中で / 〜途中に (on the way / midway through)
definition: Expresses the midway stage of moving toward a place or of an action in progress. Formed with verb dictionary form + 途中 or noun + の途中, meaning "in the middle of doing / partway along the route." 「途中で」 marks the scene where an event occurs, 「途中に」 the point during it.

spelling.text: 学校へ行く途中で、先生に会いました。

definition: I met my teacher on the way to school.

spelling.text: N／普通形 ＋ とか〜とか

patterns.title: 〜とか〜とか (such as; things like)
definition: とか lists a few representative examples and implies "there are others, too." It is close to や but more casual and colloquial, and—unlike や—it can attach to plain-form verbs and adjectives. It can even soften a single example (〜とか).

spelling.text: 休みの日は映画を見るとか買い物に行くとかします。

definition: On my days off I do things like watching movies and going shopping.

spelling.text: 〜ところだ・〜ところ（＋助詞）
〜ところ（〜るところ / 〜ているところ / 〜たところ）
V辞書形 + ところだ
Vている + ところだ
Vた形 + ところだ
〜ところで

patterns.title: About to act / Action in progress / Just completed
definition: Before: V dictionary-form + ところだ describes being just about to begin an action.
During: Vている + ところだ describes an action currently underway. A very short action may need context for a natural in-progress interpretation; a longer activity such as cooking makes the meaning clearer.
Immediately after: Vた-form + ところだ describes an action that has just finished.
Particles: ところ can take particles, as in 〜ところで, to locate another event at that stage of the action.

spelling.text: ちょうど家を出るところだったので、すぐ行けます。

definition: I was just about to leave home, so I can go right away.

spelling.text: 今から出かけるところです。

definition: I'm just about to go out now.

spelling.text: 今、家を出るところです。

definition: I'm just about to leave home.

spelling.text: 今、家を出ているところです。

definition: I'm in the process of leaving home.

spelling.text: 今、家を出たところです。

definition: I've just left home.

spelling.text: 料理しているところです。

definition: I'm in the middle of cooking.

spelling.text: 家を出るところで、電話が鳴りました。

definition: Just as I was about to leave home, the phone rang.

spelling.text: 助詞「と」の用法（共同・相互・引用・並列）

patterns.title: The particle と (together, mutual, quotation, listing)
definition: と has four main uses: (1) the partner one does something with (友だちと行く); (2) the partner of a reciprocal action (先生と話す, 彼と結婚する); (3) quotation (「はい」と言う, 行くと思う); (4) listing nouns exhaustively (パンとたまご). Listing と names all the items, whereas や gives only some examples.

spelling.text: 週末は家族と買い物に行きます。

definition: On weekends I go shopping with my family.

patterns.title: 〜は〜が、〜は〜 (contrast with は)
definition: Two elements are each marked with は and joined by が ("but"), expressing contrast. In the pattern Aは〜が、Bは〜, the differing qualities or situations of A and B are placed side by side. Here は marks contrast rather than the topic.

spelling.text: 兄は背が高いですが、弟は低いです。

definition: My older brother is tall, but my younger brother is short.

spelling.text: 数量 ＋ は（最低限の強調）

patterns.title: The particle は after a quantity ("at least")
definition: Placing は after a quantity expresses a minimum estimate, "at least that much." Whereas も marks surprise at "more than expected," quantity + は emphasizes a lower bound: "at least this much is needed / will take."

spelling.text: 駅まで歩くと、三十分はかかります。

definition: Walking to the station takes at least thirty minutes.

spelling.text: 数量 ＋ ずつ

patterns.title: 〜ずつ (each; at a time)
definition: Added after a quantity, ずつ expresses distributing an equal amount to each, or repeating the same amount each time. It covers both distribution (一人に二つずつ) and repetition/gradual progress (少しずつ覚える).

spelling.text: 子どもたちにあめを二つずつあげました。

definition: I gave the children two candies each.

spelling.text: 〜間・〜間に

patterns.title: During / While (throughout or within a period)
definition: '〜間' describes an entire period during which a state or action continues; '〜間に' marks a point within that period when a separate event occurs.

spelling.text: 子どもが寝ている間、静かにしてください。

definition: Please be quiet while the child is sleeping.

spelling.text: 〜最中（に）

patterns.title: Right in the middle of / At the height of
definition: Expresses that something happens right at the peak or deepest point of an action or state — often with a sense of interruption.

spelling.text: 会議の最中に、突然停電になった。

definition: A power outage suddenly occurred right in the middle of the meeting.

spelling.text: 〜たびに

patterns.title: Every time / Whenever
definition: Expresses that every time event X occurs, result Y invariably follows.

spelling.text: この映画を見るたびに、泣いてしまう。

definition: Every time I watch this film, I end up crying.

spelling.text: 〜て初めて

patterns.title: Only after / Not until X does one first realise/achieve Y
definition: Expresses that Y (a realisation or achievement) became possible only after experiencing X — implying Y did not exist before X.

spelling.text: 子どもを持って初めて、親の気持ちがわかった。

definition: Only after having a child did I first understand how parents feel.

spelling.text: 〜てからでないと・〜てからでなければ

patterns.title: Not until / Unless X is done first, Y cannot happen
definition: Emphasises that completing X is an indispensable prerequisite for Y — Y cannot happen unless X is done first.

spelling.text: 医者に診てもらってからでないと、薬を飲まないほうがいい。

definition: You should not take medicine unless you have seen a doctor first.

spelling.text: 〜とたん（に）

patterns.title: The instant / The moment that (Y happened right after X)
definition: Expresses that Y happened at the very instant X was completed — often unexpectedly — with no time gap between the two.

spelling.text: ドアを開けたとたん、猫が飛び出してきた。

definition: The moment I opened the door, the cat flew out.

spelling.text: 〜ついでに

patterns.title: While you are at it / Taking the opportunity to also do
definition: Expresses doing Y as a secondary action while carrying out the main purpose X — taking advantage of the opportunity.

spelling.text: スーパーに行くついでに、薬局にも寄ってきた。

definition: I stopped by the pharmacy too while I was going to the supermarket.

spelling.text: 〜うちに

patterns.title: While / Before the situation changes
definition: Expresses doing something while a certain state continues, or before it changes.

spelling.text: 熱いうちに食べてください。

definition: Please eat it while it is hot.

spelling.text: （〜ば）〜ほど・（〜なら）〜ほど

patterns.title: The more…the more
definition: Expresses proportional change: as X increases, Y increases correspondingly.

spelling.text: 練習すればするほど、上手になる。

definition: The more you practice, the better you become.

spelling.text: 〜くらい…はない・〜ほど…はない

patterns.title: Nothing is as … as X
definition: A superlative expression stating that X has the highest degree of some quality — nothing else equals or surpasses it.

spelling.text: 家族ほど大切なものはない。

definition: There is nothing as precious as family.

spelling.text: 〜くらいだ・〜ぐらいだ・〜ほどだ

patterns.title: To the extent that…; So much that…
definition: Illustrates the extreme degree or intensity of something by citing a specific extreme example or situation.

spelling.text: 昨日の試験は難しくて、泣きたくなるくらいだった。

definition: Yesterday's exam was so difficult that I felt like crying.

spelling.text: 〜くらいなら・〜ぐらいなら

patterns.title: Rather than doing X, I would…
definition: Expresses the speaker's strong preference for an alternative (Y) over an undesirable or unacceptable situation (X); 'if it comes to X, I'd rather do Y'.

spelling.text: あの人に頭を下げるくらいなら、仕事を辞めた方がましだ。

definition: I'd rather quit my job than bow my head to that person.

spelling.text: 〜に限る

patterns.title: Nothing beats X; X is the best
definition: Expresses the speaker's strong conviction or recommendation that X is the best or most appropriate option.

spelling.text: 疲れた時は、ゆっくり休むに限る。

definition: When you're tired, nothing beats resting slowly.

spelling.text: 〜に比べて

patterns.title: Compared to X
definition: A comparative expression that sets X as the reference point and describes how Y differs from it — in degree, quality, or kind.

spelling.text: 去年に比べて、今年の夏はずいぶん涼しい。

definition: Compared to last year, this summer is considerably cooler.

spelling.text: 〜にしたがって

patterns.title: As X progresses, Y changes accordingly
definition: Expresses that as X progresses or develops, Y changes naturally and inevitably in tandem.

spelling.text: 春が近づくにしたがって、気温が上がってきた。

definition: As spring approaches, the temperature has been rising.

spelling.text: 〜のわりに

patterns.title: Considering X, surprisingly Y
definition: Indicates that Y does not match what one would normally expect from X — the discrepancy can be either pleasant (better than expected) or disappointing (worse than expected).

spelling.text: 彼は年齢のわりに、ずいぶん若く見える。

definition: He looks quite young for his age.

spelling.text: 〜から・〜ことから

patterns.title: 〜ことから: basis / inference / origin
definition: 〜ことから presents fact or situation X as the basis or origin from which a judgment, name, or custom Y is derived — 'from the fact that X, Y follows.'

spelling.text: 彼女がいつも笑顔でいることから、周りの人に好かれている。

definition: From the fact that she is always smiling, it is clear she is liked by those around her.

spelling.text: 〜によって・〜による

patterns.title: 〜によって・〜による: cause / means / variation
definition: 〜によって is a multi-sense form covering: cause ('X caused Y'), means ('by means of X'), passive agent ('written by X'), and variation ('differs depending on X').

spelling.text: その建物は地震によって倒れた。

definition: The building collapsed due to the earthquake.

spelling.text: 〜によっては

patterns.title: 〜によっては: depending on the case
definition: 〜によっては signals that in some cases/conditions X, a different or exceptional result Y may occur — 'depending on X, Y can happen (though not always).'

spelling.text: この薬は人によっては副作用が出ることもある。

definition: Depending on the person, this medicine may cause side effects.

spelling.text: 〜のだから

patterns.title: 〜のだから: given that X, naturally Y
definition: 〜のだから presents fact X (which the listener knows or should know) as a strong, shared basis for a conclusion or claim Y — 'given that X, Y naturally follows / you should do Y.'

spelling.text: もう大人なのだから、自分のことは自分で決めなさい。

definition: Since you are already an adult, decide things for yourself.

spelling.text: 〜のは〜からだ・〜のは〜ためだ

patterns.title: 〜のは〜からだ / ためだ: it is because Y that X
definition: A cleft-sentence structure that explicitly foregrounds the reason: 'The reason X is (the case) is because Y' — isolating the cause Y as new, highlighted information.

spelling.text: 彼が早退したのは、頭が痛かったからだ。

definition: The reason he left early was that he had a headache.

spelling.text: 〜おかげだ・〜おかげで

patterns.title: 〜おかげで: thanks to X (positive result)
definition: 〜おかげで expresses that a positive result Y was achieved thanks to the help or good influence of X (person, thing, or circumstance).

spelling.text: 先生のおかげで、試験に合格することができました。

definition: Thanks to my teacher, I was able to pass the exam.

spelling.text: 〜せいだ・〜せいで

patterns.title: 〜せいで: because of X (negative result / blame)
definition: 〜せいで attributes an undesirable or negative result Y to the fault or bad influence of X — carrying a nuance of blame or dissatisfaction.

spelling.text: 雨のせいで、試合が中止になってしまった。

definition: The match ended up being cancelled because of the rain.

spelling.text: 〜ためだ・〜ため（に）

patterns.title: 〜ため(に): cause / purpose
definition: 〜ために expresses either a cause/reason (something happened because of X) or a purpose (do Y in order to do X), depending on context.

spelling.text: 台風のために、試合が中止になった。

definition: The match was cancelled because of the typhoon.

spelling.text: 〜反面

patterns.title: On the other hand / conversely ~
definition: Presents the flip side of the same subject: while X is true of something, Y (the opposite) is also true.

spelling.text: この薬は効果が高い反面、副作用も強い。

definition: This medicine is highly effective; on the other hand, its side effects are also strong.

spelling.text: いくら〜ても・どんなに〜ても

patterns.title: No matter how much ~ / however ~
definition: Emphasizes that no matter how extreme the degree or quantity in the first clause, the result or state in the second clause remains unchanged.

spelling.text: いくら練習しても、なかなかうまくならない。

definition: No matter how much I practice, I just can't seem to improve.

spelling.text: 〜一方（で）

patterns.title: On one hand ~ / while ~
definition: Presents two parallel but different facts or situations; the subjects may be the same or different.

spelling.text: スマートフォンは生活を便利にした一方で、人々の集中力を低下させたともいわれている。

definition: Smartphones have made life more convenient; on the other hand, they are also said to have reduced people's concentration.

spelling.text: 〜かわりに・〜にかわって

patterns.title: Instead of ~ / in place of ~ / in return for ~
definition: Has two main uses: ① substitution (do Y instead of X) and ② compensation/exchange (do Y in return for X). にかわって is primarily used for replacing a person or position.

spelling.text: 今日は田中さんのかわりに、私が会議に出席します。

definition: I will attend the meeting in place of Mr. Tanaka today.

spelling.text: 〜くせに

patterns.title: Even though ~ (reproachful)
definition: Expresses the speaker's reproach, contempt, or criticism toward someone whose behavior in the second clause contradicts the fact stated in the first. Much stronger in emotional charge than のに.

spelling.text: 何も知らないくせに、偉そうなことを言わないでよ。

definition: Don't act so high and mighty when you don't know anything.

spelling.text: 〜ものの

patterns.title: Although ~ / even though ~ (written concession)
definition: A concessive connective that acknowledges the fact in the first clause while presenting a contradictory or disappointing second clause. Carries a formal/written nuance.

spelling.text: 試験には合格したものの、成績はあまりよくなかった。

definition: Although I passed the exam, my score was not very good.

spelling.text: 〜に対して

patterns.title: In contrast to / toward ~
definition: Contrasts two things or people, showing that X and Y differ in some way.

spelling.text: 姉は社交的なのに対して、弟はとても内気だ。

definition: My older sister is sociable, whereas my younger brother is very shy.

spelling.text: たとえ〜ても・たとえ〜でも

patterns.title: Even if ~ / no matter ~
definition: Presents a hypothetical or extreme situation and emphasizes that the outcome or attitude in the second clause will not change regardless.

spelling.text: たとえ失敗しても、もう一度挑戦するつもりだ。

definition: Even if I fail, I intend to try again.

spelling.text: 〜というより

patterns.title: Rather than saying ~ / more accurately ~
definition: States that the second expression is more accurate or appropriate than the first; it does not deny the first but refines it.

spelling.text: 彼の話し方は説明というより、命令に近い。

definition: His way of speaking is less an explanation and more like giving orders.

spelling.text: 〜ずに

patterns.title: Without doing ~ / instead of doing ~
definition: Indicates that the action in the second clause is performed without doing the action in the first clause. Nearly synonymous with 〜ないで but carries a more formal/written register.

spelling.text: 彼は何も言わずに部屋を出て行った。

definition: He left the room without saying a word.

spelling.text: 〜ば・〜たら・〜なら（反実仮想）

patterns.title: ば vs たら vs なら: comparison and counterfactuals
definition: Organizes the distinctions between ば, たら, and なら as conditional forms, focusing especially on their use in counterfactual (contrary-to-fact) hypotheticals.

spelling.text: 春になれば、桜が咲く。

definition: When spring comes (whenever spring comes), the cherry blossoms bloom. [ば for general law]

spelling.text: 〜ばよかった・〜たらよかった

patterns.title: 〜ばよかった・〜たらよかった: regretful counterfactual
definition: Expresses regret or disappointment: 'I wish I had done X (but I didn't)' or 'I wish I hadn't done X (but I did)'.

spelling.text: もっと早く起きればよかった。電車に乗り遅れてしまった。

definition: I wish I had gotten up earlier. I missed the train.

spelling.text: もし〜たら・もし〜なら

patterns.title: もし〜たら・もし〜なら: emphasizing hypothesis
definition: Adding もし (=if, supposing) emphasizes that the condition is uncertain or has a low probability of occurring.

spelling.text: もし宝くじに当たったら、世界旅行に行きたい。

definition: If I won the lottery, I would want to travel the world.

spelling.text: もし〜としても

patterns.title: もし〜としても: hypothetical concession
definition: Expresses a hypothetical concession: 'even supposing/assuming X were the case, the result/conclusion would still be the same'.

spelling.text: もし彼が謝ったとしても、もう信じることはできない。

definition: Even if he were to apologize, I can no longer trust him.

spelling.text: 〜（の）なら

patterns.title: 〜(の)なら: conditional on a given topic
definition: Expresses a condition based on information just received or assumed: 'if that is indeed the case / if you mean X'.

spelling.text: 東京に行くなら、スカイツリーに寄ってみてください。

definition: If you're going to Tokyo, please stop by the Skytree.

spelling.text: 〜さえ〜ば・〜さえ〜なら

patterns.title: 〜さえ〜ば／なら: minimal sufficient condition
definition: Expresses that satisfying one minimal condition is sufficient ('as long as / just X is enough'), implying no other conditions are needed.

spelling.text: お金さえあれば、その問題は解決できる。

definition: As long as we have money, that problem can be solved.

spelling.text: 〜たところ

patterns.title: 〜たところ: result or discovery upon doing
definition: Expresses that as a result of doing something, a new fact or situation came to light: 'upon doing X, it turned out that Y'.

spelling.text: 先生に聞いてみたところ、明日は休みだとわかった。

definition: When I asked the teacher, I found out that tomorrow is a holiday.

spelling.text: 〜ては・〜（の）では

patterns.title: 〜ては／〜(の)では: condition leading to a bad outcome
definition: Expresses criticism, concern, or warning that if a certain action or state continues, a bad result will follow.

spelling.text: 毎日遅刻しては、上司に怒られても仕方ない。

definition: If you keep being late every day, it's no wonder your boss gets angry.

spelling.text: 〜ところだった

patterns.title: 〜ところだった: nearly happened / narrowly avoided
definition: Expresses that something nearly happened (but didn't, in the relief/scare usage) or that something just barely happened. Often conveys a close call, narrow escape, or near-miss.

spelling.text: もう少しで電車に乗り遅れるところだった。

definition: I nearly missed the train (but made it).

spelling.text: 〜としたら・〜とすれば

patterns.title: 〜としたら・〜とすれば: hypothetical reasoning
definition: Expresses logical or thought-experiment hypothesis: 'if we assume/suppose X to be the case, what conclusion or inference follows?'

spelling.text: もし彼女が犯人だとしたら、動機は何だろう。

definition: If she were the culprit, what would the motive be?

spelling.text: 〜と…た（直後の動作）

patterns.title: 〜と…た: immediate next action
definition: Expresses that immediately upon the completion of the prior action or event, the speaker performed the next action (or an event occurred instantly).

spelling.text: 授業が終わると、すぐに友達に電話した。

definition: As soon as class ended, I immediately called my friend.

spelling.text: 〜と…た・〜たら…た（発見）

patterns.title: 〜と…た・〜たら…た: unexpected discovery
definition: Describes discovering an unexpected situation or fact at the moment of performing an action or moving somewhere (narrative of a past experience).

spelling.text: 玄関を開けると、大きな犬がいた。

definition: When I opened the front door, there was a big dog.

spelling.text: なぜ〜かというと、〜からだ

patterns.title: The reason why… is because…
definition: A structure that emphasises a reason: the 「なぜ〜かというと」part raises the question 'why', and 「〜からだ」answers it.

spelling.text: なぜ毎朝運動するかというと、健康を維持したいからだ。

definition: The reason I exercise every morning is that I want to maintain my health.

spelling.text: 〜といった

patterns.title: Such as… / Like…
definition: Lists examples to represent a broader category; similar to「などの」but slightly more formal/written.

spelling.text: 東京や大阪といった大都市では、家賃が高い。

definition: In large cities such as Tokyo and Osaka, rents are high.

spelling.text: 〜ということだ・〜とのことだ

patterns.title: It means that… / I heard that…
definition: Expresses hearsay (one has obtained information that…) or a logical conclusion (it amounts to the fact that…).

spelling.text: 天気予報によると、明日は大雨になるということだ。

definition: According to the weather forecast, it seems it will rain heavily tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜という＋名詞

patterns.title: …called / known as…
definition: Modifies a noun to identify, name, or define it: 'a [noun] called…' or 'the [noun] that says…'.

spelling.text: 「一期一会」という言葉は、一生に一度の出会いを大切にするという意味だ。

definition: The phrase "ichi-go ichi-e" means cherishing a once-in-a-lifetime encounter.

spelling.text: 〜というのは

patterns.title: What … means is… / The thing called… is…
definition: Takes up a word, concept, or situation and provides a definition or explanation; slightly more conversational than「〜とは」.

spelling.text: 「侘び寂び」というのは、日本の美意識の一つで、不完全さや無常の中に美を見出すことだ。

definition: "Wabi-sabi" is one of Japan's aesthetic sensibilities — finding beauty in imperfection and impermanence.

spelling.text: 〜というと

patterns.title: Speaking of… / When you say…
definition: Used when hearing a topic triggers an association — 'speaking of X, (I think of) Y'.

spelling.text: 日本の夏というと、やはり花火大会を思い浮かべる。

definition: When I think of Japanese summer, fireworks festivals naturally come to mind.

spelling.text: 〜と言われている

patterns.title: It is said that… / It is believed that…
definition: Expresses something widely believed or commonly said among people in general.

spelling.text: 緑茶には健康に良い成分が多く含まれていると言われている。

definition: Green tea is said to contain many ingredients that are beneficial to health.

spelling.text: 〜とか

patterns.title: I heard that… (vague hearsay)
definition: A casual expression conveying uncertain or vague hearsay, often with a nuance of 'I'm not quite sure but I heard that…'.

spelling.text: 田中さん、来週結婚するとか。

definition: I heard something about Tanaka-san getting married next week.

spelling.text: 〜って（伝聞・口語）

patterns.title: I heard that… / So-called… (casual)
definition: A casual spoken contraction of「〜と」used for hearsay ('I heard that…') or to introduce a topic ('Speaking of…').

spelling.text: 山田さん、明日休みだって。

definition: I heard Yamada-san is off tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜ように言う・〜と頼まれる（間接話法）

patterns.title: Tell someone to… / Be asked to… (reported request)
definition: In reported speech, commands or requests are conveyed not as direct quotes but using「〜ように」to paraphrase.

spelling.text: 先生は学生たちに、毎日30分は日本語を練習するように言った。

definition: The teacher told the students to practise Japanese for at least 30 minutes every day.

spelling.text: 必ずしも〜とは限らない

patterns.title: Not necessarily ~
definition: Combines the adverb 必ずしも with とは限らない to strongly emphasize that something is not always the case.

spelling.text: お金があれば必ずしも幸せになれるとは限らない。

definition: Having money doesn't necessarily mean you'll be happy.

spelling.text: 決して〜ない・少しも〜ない・めったに〜ない

patterns.title: Never ~ / Not at all ~ / Rarely ~
definition: Negative-polarity adverbs (決して, 少しも, めったに) that must pair with a negative predicate to express strong or emphatic negation.

spelling.text: この秘密は決して誰にも話さない。

definition: I will never tell this secret to anyone.

spelling.text: 〜ことは〜が

patterns.title: ~ is true, but ~
definition: Concedes a fact in the first clause, then introduces a contrasting point, limitation, or dissatisfaction in the second.

spelling.text: 彼の説明はわかることはわかるが、賛成できない。

definition: I do understand his explanation, but I can't agree with it.

spelling.text: 〜ことはない

patterns.title: There's no need to ~
definition: Expresses that there is no need or necessity to do something.

spelling.text: そんなに心配することはない。きっとうまくいくよ。

definition: There's no need to worry so much. I'm sure it'll work out.

spelling.text: 〜ないことはない・〜ないこともない

patterns.title: It's not that ~ cannot / It's possible (if pressed)
definition: Double negation that indirectly affirms possibility or willingness, but with a lukewarm or reluctant nuance.

spelling.text: 一人で行けないことはないが、できれば誰かと一緒に行きたい。

definition: It's not that I can't go alone, but I'd prefer to go with someone if possible.

spelling.text: 〜しかない

patterns.title: Have no choice but to ~ / Only ~
definition: Expresses that there is no other option left — one has no choice but to do something, or only one thing remains.

spelling.text: 電車が止まっているから、歩くしかない。

definition: The trains are stopped, so we have no choice but to walk.

spelling.text: 〜しかたがない・〜しょうがない

patterns.title: Can't be helped / No way around it
definition: ① Expresses resignation that a situation cannot be changed. ② Also expresses an irresistibly strong feeling or urge (〜てしかたがない).

spelling.text: 試験に落ちてしまった。しかたがない、また来年頑張ろう。

definition: I failed the exam. Oh well, I can't help it — I'll try again next year.

spelling.text: 〜とは限らない

patterns.title: Not necessarily ~
definition: Expresses partial negation, meaning 'it is not always the case that ~' or 'there are exceptions.'

spelling.text: 高い薬が必ずしも効くとは限らない。

definition: Expensive medicine is not necessarily effective.

spelling.text: 〜わけではない・〜というわけではない

patterns.title: It's not that ~ / Not exactly ~
definition: Partially denies a misunderstanding or assumption, meaning 'it's not that ~ / it doesn't mean that ~.'

spelling.text: 日本語が話せないわけではないが、ネイティブほど流暢ではない。

definition: It's not that I can't speak Japanese — it's just that I'm not as fluent as a native speaker.

spelling.text: 〜べきだ・〜べきではない

patterns.title: Should / Shouldn't (moral obligation)
definition: Expresses a moral or social obligation; what one ought to do from a normative standpoint.

spelling.text: 困っている人を見たら、助けるべきだと思う。

definition: I think you should help people who are in trouble.

spelling.text: 〜ことだ

patterns.title: The best thing to do is / You should (advice)
definition: Used to give advice, meaning 'the best thing to do is X' or 'you should X'.

spelling.text: 体を丈夫にしたいなら、毎日運動することだ。

definition: If you want to be healthy, the best thing is to exercise every day.

spelling.text: 〜こと（指示・規則）

patterns.title: Must do (written rule / instruction)
definition: A written-language expression commanding or instructing that something must be done, as in rules or notices.

spelling.text: 試験中は辞書を使わないこと。

definition: During the exam, do not use a dictionary.

spelling.text: 〜ものだ（本来・回想）

patterns.title: That's how things are / Used to (general truth & reminiscence)
definition: States a general or universal truth about how things naturally are, or recalls past habits with nostalgia.

spelling.text: 人間というものは、いつか死ぬものだ。

definition: Human beings are something that must eventually die — that's the nature of things.

spelling.text: 〜ないわけにはいかない

patterns.title: Cannot help but do / Must do
definition: Expresses that one must do something due to social or moral reasons; a double-negative 'cannot not do'.

spelling.text: 親友が困っているなら、助けないわけにはいかない。

definition: If my best friend is in trouble, I simply must help them.

spelling.text: 〜つもりでした（未実現）

patterns.title: Had intended to (but didn't)
definition: Expresses a past intention or plan that was not realized in the end.

spelling.text: 早く帰るつもりでしたが、仕事が終わらなくて遅くなってしまいました。

definition: I had intended to go home early, but work didn't finish and I ended up being late.

spelling.text: 〜わけだ・〜というわけだ

patterns.title: That's why / No wonder
definition: Expresses a logical conclusion drawn from known facts; 'no wonder', 'so that's why'.

spelling.text: 彼は10年間日本に住んでいるから、日本語が上手なわけだ。

definition: He's lived in Japan for 10 years, so no wonder his Japanese is good.

spelling.text: 〜わけにはいかない

patterns.title: Can't possibly do / Mustn't do
definition: Expresses that one cannot do something due to social, psychological, or moral constraints, even if one wants to.

spelling.text: 大切な試験があるので、今日は休むわけにはいかない。

definition: I have an important exam, so I can't possibly take the day off.

spelling.text: 命令（しろ）・禁止（〜な）

patterns.title: Imperative (do it!) / Prohibitive (don't do it!)
definition: The imperative (命令形) issues a strong direct command; the prohibitive 「〜な」 orders someone NOT to do something. Both are blunt, typically used by males or toward subordinates/children — not in polite or formal contexts.

spelling.text: 火事だ！早く逃げろ！

definition: Fire! Run away quickly!

spelling.text: 〜ないと・〜なくては

patterns.title: Must / Have to (or else)
definition: Colloquial contraction of 〜しなければならない, expressing obligation or necessity. The consequence clause (〜ならない / いけない / ダメ) is often omitted in speech.

spelling.text: 明日、試験があるから、今夜しっかり勉強しないと。

definition: I have an exam tomorrow, so I have to study properly tonight.

spelling.text: 〜（さ）せてもらいたい・〜（さ）せてほしい

patterns.title: Want to be allowed to do X
definition: Expresses the speaker's desire to be permitted to do something, essentially asking for the other person's consent or allowance.

spelling.text: この件は私に担当させてほしいんですが。

definition: I'd like to be the one to handle this matter.

spelling.text: 〜てごらん

patterns.title: Try doing X and see (gentle suggestion)
definition: A gentle encouragement for someone (typically a child or subordinate, from a parent, teacher, or senior) to try something and see what happens. 「ごらん」 derives from the honorific 「御覧」 but now functions as a soft imperative.

spelling.text: 難しくないよ。一度やってごらん。

definition: It's not hard. Try doing it once.

spelling.text: 〜といい・〜ばいい・〜たらいい

patterns.title: Should do X / It would be good to do X (advice)
definition: Advises or suggests that a certain action would be good or would solve a problem; can express recommendation or a softer 'all you have to do is…' nuance.

spelling.text: 疲れたら少し休んだらいいよ。

definition: If you're tired, you should take a little rest.

spelling.text: 〜といいなあ・〜ないかなあ

patterns.title: I hope / I wish (soft personal wish)
definition: Expresses the speaker's soft personal wish or hope with the sentence-final particle なあ, giving a wistful or muttering tone with no guarantee of fulfilment.

spelling.text: 明日、晴れるといいなあ。

definition: I hope it's sunny tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜ようとしない

patterns.title: Refuse to / Won't even try to
definition: Expresses that the subject deliberately refuses to do something or won't even make an attempt.

spelling.text: 彼はどんなに説明しても、考えを変えようとしない。

definition: No matter how much I explain, he refuses to change his mind.

spelling.text: 〜（よ）うとする

patterns.title: Be about to / Try to do
definition: Expresses the moment just before an action is taken, or an attempt to carry out an action.

spelling.text: 家を出ようとしたとき、急に雨が降り始めた。

definition: Just as I was about to leave home, it suddenly started raining.

spelling.text: 〜だらけだ

patterns.title: Covered in / Full of (negative)
definition: Expresses a state where something undesirable is present everywhere or covers the entire surface; inherently negative in nuance.

spelling.text: この作文は間違いだらけだ。

definition: This composition is full of mistakes.

spelling.text: 〜ふりをする

patterns.title: Pretend to / Act as if
definition: Expresses the act of pretending or feigning a state or action that does not reflect reality.

spelling.text: 彼は私を見かけたのに、知らないふりをした。

definition: He pretended not to know me even though he saw me.

spelling.text: 〜（かの）ようだ・〜（かの）ように

patterns.title: As if / Just as though
definition: A figurative or literary expression describing something as if it were a certain way, even though it is not actually so.

spelling.text: 彼女は何も知らないかのように振る舞っていた。

definition: She was behaving as if she knew nothing (even though she did).

spelling.text: まるで〜よう

patterns.title: Just like / Exactly as if
definition: 「まるで」pairs with 「ようだ/ように/みたいだ」to intensify a simile or hypothetical description, meaning 'just like' or 'exactly as if'.

spelling.text: 彼女の歌声はまるで天使のようだ。

definition: Her singing voice is just like an angel's.

spelling.text: もしかしたら〜かもしれない

patterns.title: Maybe / Perhaps X might be the case
definition: A weak possibility expression in which the adverb 「もしかしたら」(perhaps/possibly) must co-occur with 「かもしれない」(might be).

spelling.text: もしかしたら、彼はもう知っているかもしれない。

definition: Perhaps he might already know.

spelling.text: 〜っぽい

patterns.title: -ish / Tends to be
definition: A colloquial expression meaning something has a certain quality, tendency, or appearance, often implying it is not quite the real thing.

spelling.text: 彼の話し方はちょっと子供っぽいね。

definition: His way of speaking is a bit childish.

spelling.text: 〜のようだ・〜みたいだ

patterns.title: Seems like / Looks like
definition: Expresses the speaker's conjecture based on direct observation or experience; みたいだ is the casual equivalent of ようだ.

spelling.text: 空が暗い。雨が降るようだ。

definition: The sky is dark. It looks like it will rain.

spelling.text: 〜ばかり（限定）

patterns.title: Nothing but X / Always only X
definition: Expresses a state where X is overwhelmingly predominant with little else; carries a nuance of excess or bias, stronger than だけ.

spelling.text: 弟は甘いものばかり食べて、ご飯を全然食べない。

definition: My younger brother eats nothing but sweets and won't eat proper meals at all.

spelling.text: 〜ばかりか〜も

patterns.title: Not only X but also Y
definition: Expresses that something extends beyond X to include Y as well; Y carries a nuance of surprise, unexpectedness, or added emphasis.

spelling.text: 彼女は日本語ばかりか、中国語も流暢に話せる。

definition: She can speak not only Japanese but also Chinese fluently.

spelling.text: 〜だけしか〜ない

patterns.title: Nothing but X — emphatic
definition: Stacks だけ and しか〜ない to emphatically state that nothing other than X exists or is available — stronger than either alone.

spelling.text: 財布に五百円だけしか入っていなかった。

definition: There was only ¥500 in my wallet — nothing more.

spelling.text: 〜でも

patterns.title: でも — even / for example
definition: Expresses either 'even X (without exception)' as inclusive emphasis, or a light suggestion meaning 'X, for example / or something like X'.

spelling.text: この仕事は誰でもできる簡単なものではない。

definition: This job is not something that just anyone can do.

spelling.text: 〜ぐらい・くらい

patterns.title: ぐらい・くらい — approximately / only this much
definition: Has two main uses: (1) approximate quantity/degree 'about, around'; (2) minimal/contemptuous degree 'at least X / even just X / something as simple as X'.

spelling.text: この作業には、30分ぐらいかかると思います。

definition: I think this task will take about 30 minutes.

spelling.text: 〜っきり・〜きり

patterns.title: Only X, nothing since / Just X and that's it
definition: ① Limits quantity or action to just X (きり①). ② Expresses that since a certain action/state, nothing has changed — the situation has continued or no further contact/occurrence has happened (きり②).

spelling.text: あの人とは一度会ったきり、連絡が取れていない。

definition: I met that person just once, and since then I haven't been able to contact them.

spelling.text: 〜こそ

patterns.title: こそ — emphatic 'precisely'
definition: Emphasises that something is exactly the right thing; 'it is precisely X', 'X is the very one'.

spelling.text: 今年こそ、日本語能力試験に合格してみせる。

definition: This year, of all years, I will show everyone I can pass the JLPT.

spelling.text: 〜まで（強調）

patterns.title: まで — even (beyond expectation)
definition: Emphasises that something extends even to an unexpected or extreme point; 'even X (which one would not have imagined)'.

spelling.text: 彼はひどく落ち込んで、食事まで忘れるほどだった。

definition: He was so depressed that he even forgot to eat.

spelling.text: 〜も（強調）

patterns.title: も — as many/much as (emphatic quantity)
definition: Emphasises that a quantity or degree is surprisingly large (or small), conveying the speaker's astonishment: 'as many/much as X'.

spelling.text: この本は5回も読んだのに、まだ内容を覚えていない。

definition: I have read this book as many as five times, yet I still cannot remember the content.

spelling.text: 〜など・なんか

patterns.title: など・なんか — such as / (belittling)
definition: など gives examples ('things like X, such as X'); なんか is the colloquial form and additionally carries the speaker's belittling attitude ('something as insignificant as X') or self-deprecation.

spelling.text: 休みの日は、映画や音楽などを楽しみます。

definition: On days off, I enjoy things like movies and music.

spelling.text: 〜さえ

patterns.title: さえ — even / as long as (extreme example)
definition: Presents an extreme example to mean 'even X (which is the last thing expected)'; or in 〜さえ〜ば, states the minimum sufficient condition 'as long as / if only X'.

spelling.text: 彼は疲れていたのか、食事さえとらずに眠ってしまった。

definition: He was so tired that he fell asleep without even eating.

spelling.text: 〜はもちろん〜も

patterns.title: X of course, and Y too
definition: States that X goes without saying, and that Y is additionally true. X is presented as an obvious given or natural expectation; Y is the highlighted addition.

spelling.text: この料理は見た目はもちろん、味も最高だ。

definition: This dish is of course beautiful to look at, but the taste is also outstanding.

spelling.text: 〜に関して

patterns.title: Regarding / With Regard To
definition: A formal expression meaning "regarding" or "with regard to", primarily used in written or formal spoken contexts.

spelling.text: この件に関して、詳しく説明します。

definition: I will explain this matter in detail.

spelling.text: 〜において

patterns.title: In / At / In the Context Of (Formal)
definition: A formal expression indicating place, time, situation, or field, roughly equivalent to "in", "at", or "in the context of". Primarily written/formal.

spelling.text: この会議は東京において開催されます。

definition: This conference will be held in Tokyo.

spelling.text: 〜にとって

patterns.title: For / From the Standpoint Of
definition: Expresses an evaluation or impression from a particular person's or group's point of view, meaning "for" or "from the perspective of".

spelling.text: この仕事は私にとって大きなチャンスです。

definition: This job is a big opportunity for me.

spelling.text: 〜について

patterns.title: About / Concerning
definition: Used to indicate the topic or subject being discussed, meaning "about" or "concerning" something.

spelling.text: 日本の文化について調べています。

definition: I am researching Japanese culture.

spelling.text: 〜によると

patterns.title: According To
definition: Indicates the source of information, meaning "according to (source X)". Often followed by そうだ or らしい (hearsay/conjecture endings).

spelling.text: 天気予報によると、明日は雨が降るそうです。

definition: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

spelling.text: 〜として・〜にしては

patterns.title: As / In the Capacity Of — For / Considering
definition: として expresses role, capacity, or identity; にしては expresses a result unexpected given a stated premise or identity.

spelling.text: 彼は日本語の教師として働いています。

definition: He works as a Japanese language teacher.

spelling.text: 〜こと vs 〜の（名詞化）

patterns.title: こと vs の — clause nominalization
definition: Both こと and の turn a verb/adjective clause into a noun; の is used for sensory or concrete events, こと for abstract concepts and set phrases.

spelling.text: 彼女が泣いているのが見えた。

definition: I could see that she was crying. (direct perception → の)

spelling.text: 〜ますように

patterns.title: 〜ますように — I wish / I pray that X happens
definition: Expresses the speaker's heartfelt wish or prayer that something will happen (Please let it be that…, I hope that…).

spelling.text: 試験に合格しますように。

definition: I hope / pray that I pass the exam.

spelling.text: 〜み（形容詞の名詞化）

patterns.title: 〜み — adjective nominalization (subjective feeling/quality)
definition: Attach み to the stem of an i-adjective to form a noun expressing subjective feeling, sentiment, or texture — more emotional and internal than さ.

spelling.text: 旅行を楽しみにしています。

definition: I'm looking forward to the trip. (anticipation set phrase → 楽しみ)

spelling.text: 〜のように・〜のような

patterns.title: 〜のように / のような — like X (comparison/example)
definition: Noun + のように/のような expresses comparison or exemplification (like X, such as X); のように modifies verbs and adjectives, のような modifies nouns.

spelling.text: 彼女は鳥のように自由に生きている。

definition: She lives freely like a bird. (simile → のように)

spelling.text: 〜さ（形容詞の名詞化）

patterns.title: 〜さ — adjective nominalization (measurable degree)
definition: Attach さ to the stem of an i-adjective or na-adjective to form a noun expressing an objectively measurable degree or quality.

spelling.text: この山の高さは3776メートルです。

definition: The height of this mountain is 3,776 metres. (measurable → さ)

spelling.text: 〜ように（基準・既知の前置き）

patterns.title: 〜ように — as you know / as stated (standard/known reference)
definition: Use ように to preface a statement with shared or previously established information (as you know, as I mentioned, as expected).

spelling.text: ご存知のように、来月から新しいルールが適用されます。

definition: As you know, new rules will be applied from next month. (known-info preface → ように kijun)

spelling.text: 〜ようになっている

patterns.title: 〜ようになっている — designed/set up so that X happens
definition: Expresses that something is designed, set up, or structured so that a certain outcome occurs — an intentional system or arrangement.

spelling.text: このドアは自動的に閉まるようになっている。

definition: This door is designed to close automatically. (mechanical system)

spelling.text: 〜ようにと（要求・指示）

patterns.title: 〜ようにと — told / asked to (indirect instruction)
definition: Conveys instructions, requests, or demands made to a third party indirectly; typical forms include 〜ように（と）言う, 伝える, 頼む.

spelling.text: 先生は早く寝るようにと言った。

definition: The teacher told (us) to go to bed early. (indirect instruction → ようにと)

spelling.text: 〜上げる・〜上がる

patterns.title: Finish completely / bring to completion
definition: Expresses bringing an action to full completion, with the result fully realized.

spelling.text: 三年かけて、やっと小説を書き上げた。

definition: After three years, I finally finished writing the novel.

spelling.text: 〜ばかりだ（一方向変化）

patterns.title: Just keeps getting more X
definition: Indicates that a situation keeps changing in one direction with no prospect of improvement, often with a pessimistic or lamenting tone.

spelling.text: 最近、仕事が忙しくなるばかりで、休む暇もない。

definition: Lately, work just keeps getting busier and there is no time to rest.

spelling.text: 〜ばかりでなく

patterns.title: Not only X but also
definition: Expresses that not only X but also Y is the case, adding or expanding beyond X. A more emphatic or written-register form of だけでなく.

spelling.text: この映画は日本ばかりでなく、世界中で人気がある。

definition: This film is popular not only in Japan but all over the world.

spelling.text: 〜出す

patterns.title: Suddenly start doing
definition: Expresses that an action or state suddenly and spontaneously begins.

spelling.text: 映画の悲しいシーンで、彼女は突然泣き出した。

definition: At the sad scene in the film, she suddenly burst into tears.

spelling.text: 〜がちだ

patterns.title: Tend to / prone to
definition: Indicates a tendency for something undesirable to happen repeatedly, or a negative inclination deeply ingrained in a person or thing.

spelling.text: 彼は忙しくて、食事を抜きがちだ。

definition: He is busy and tends to skip meals.

spelling.text: 〜かける・〜かけだ

patterns.title: Half-done / In the middle of doing
definition: Indicates an action was started but left unfinished or is partway done.

spelling.text: 読みかけの本をそのままにして出かけてしまった。

definition: I left the half-read book as it was and went out.

spelling.text: 〜きる

patterns.title: Do completely / to the very end
definition: Indicates an action is carried out completely, thoroughly, or to the very end.

spelling.text: マラソンを最後まで走りきった。

definition: I ran the marathon all the way to the end.

spelling.text: 〜っぱなし

patterns.title: Left doing X / left undone
definition: Expresses that the resulting state of an action has been left as is — what should have been stopped, closed, or put back remains neglected — often with a critical or lamenting tone.

spelling.text: 窓を開けっぱなしにしないでください。虫が入りますよ。

definition: Please don't leave the window open. Insects will get in.

spelling.text: 〜たばかりだ

patterns.title: Just did X / just finished
definition: Indicates that an action was completed just a short time ago — very recently finished.

spelling.text: 今、昼ご飯を食べたばかりだから、まだおなかがいっぱい。

definition: I just had lunch so I'm still full.

spelling.text: 〜たての・〜たて

patterns.title: Freshly done / just completed
definition: Expresses the state immediately after an action is completed, when it is still fresh.

spelling.text: 焼きたてのパンはとてもおいしい。

definition: Freshly baked bread is really delicious.

spelling.text: 〜てばかりいる

patterns.title: Do nothing but X
definition: Expresses that someone does nothing but a certain action, repeatedly, often with a critical or lamenting tone.

spelling.text: 弟はゲームをしてばかりいて、全然勉強しない。

definition: My younger brother does nothing but play games and never studies at all.

spelling.text: 〜通す

patterns.title: Do throughout / persevere to the end
definition: Expresses doing something consistently from start to finish, often despite obstacles.

spelling.text: どんなに批判されても、自分の意見を言い通した。

definition: No matter how much I was criticized, I kept stating my opinion.

spelling.text: 〜づらい

patterns.title: Hard/painful to do
definition: Expresses subjective difficulty—psychological or physical reluctance that makes an action hard or painful to carry out.

spelling.text: 彼女のことを傷つけるようなことは、言いづらかった。

definition: It was painful to say something that might hurt her.

spelling.text: 自動詞・他動詞の使い分け

patterns.title: Intransitive vs. Transitive Verbs
definition: Intransitive verbs describe the subject changing or acting on its own (no external agent implied); transitive verbs describe a subject acting upon an object — shifting the perspective between natural change vs. deliberate action.

spelling.text: 風でドアが開いた。／私がドアを開けた。

definition: Intransitive: The door opened because of the wind (natural change). / Transitive: I opened the door (deliberate action).

spelling.text: 使役（〜させる）

patterns.title: Causative Form (~させる)
definition: Expresses that the speaker causes, permits, or allows someone else to do something — covering coercion, permission, and letting someone act freely.

spelling.text: 先生は学生に作文を書かせた。

definition: Coercion: The teacher made the students write an essay.

spelling.text: 使役受身（〜させられる）

patterns.title: Causative-Passive (~させられる)
definition: Expresses that the subject was made to do something against their will — emphasizes unwillingness or being forced by an external party.

spelling.text: 毎日上司に残業させられた。

definition: Reluctant: I was made to work overtime every day by my boss (against my will).

spelling.text: 〜てあげる

patterns.title: Do ~ for someone (giving benefit outward)
definition: A benefit-giving expression where the speaker (or in-group member) does something for another person (out-group); the action flows outward from the giver.

spelling.text: 友達に道を教えてあげた。

definition: I told my friend the way (I gave the benefit of directions to my friend).

spelling.text: 〜てくれる

patterns.title: Do ~ for me (giver volunteers benefit inward)
definition: Expresses that someone (out-group) voluntarily performs an action for the speaker or in-group — the giver is the grammatical subject and the benefit flows inward. Conveys the speaker's appreciation.

spelling.text: 友達が荷物を持ってくれた。

definition: My friend voluntarily carried my luggage (I am grateful).

spelling.text: 〜てもらう

patterns.title: Have someone do ~ (receiving benefit inward)
definition: Expresses that the speaker (or in-group) receives a benefit by having someone else perform an action — the action flows inward toward the receiver.

spelling.text: 友達に荷物を運んでもらった。

definition: I had my friend carry my luggage (I received that benefit).

spelling.text: 受身（〜られる）

patterns.title: Passive Form (~られる)
definition: Expresses that the subject receives or is affected by an action — covers both direct passive and indirect/suffering passive.

spelling.text: 私は先生に名前を呼ばれた。

definition: Direct passive: The teacher called my name (and I received that action).

spelling.text: だけど・ですから

patterns.title: だけど・ですから — but / so (colloquial)
definition: Colloquial conjunctions frequently used in everyday conversation. だけど (but / though) is the casual spoken equivalent of でも / しかし; ですから (so / that is why) is the polite spoken equivalent of だから, introducing a conclusion or request based on a stated reason.

spelling.text: 行きたい。だけど、時間がない。

definition: I want to go. But I don't have time.

spelling.text: こ・そ・あ（指示語）

patterns.title: こ・そ・あ — discourse demonstratives
definition: The Japanese demonstrative system (ko-so-a-do). In conversation, selection depends on physical distance from speaker/listener. In written discourse, selection depends on information distance within the text: こ (ko-series) refers to what was just stated in the same text; そ (so-series) refers to information known to the listener or mentioned slightly earlier; あ (a-series) refers to shared memory or common knowledge between speaker and listener.

spelling.text: 新しい規則が発表された。この規則は来月から適用される。

definition: A new rule has been announced. This rule will take effect from next month.

spelling.text: または・それとも

patterns.title: または・それとも — or / or else
definition: Disjunctive conjunctions presenting two or more alternatives. または (or / alternatively) is used in written language and declarative statements to present options neutrally; それとも (or / or else) is used in spoken language and questions to ask which of two options applies.

spelling.text: 申し込みは窓口、またはウェブサイトからできます。

definition: Applications can be submitted at the counter or through the website.

spelling.text: そのため・したがって・そこで

patterns.title: そのため・したがって・そこで — therefore / consequently / so then
definition: Sentence-initial conjunctions that introduce a result or action caused by what preceded. そのため (for that reason / because of that) states an objective causal link; したがって (therefore / accordingly) signals logical deduction in formal writing; そこで (so / that being the case) introduces a decision or action taken in response to the situation.

spelling.text: 台風が近づいている。そのため、イベントは中止になった。

definition: A typhoon is approaching. For that reason, the event was cancelled.

spelling.text: そのうえ・さらに・しかも

patterns.title: そのうえ・さらに・しかも — moreover / furthermore / what is more
definition: Additive conjunctions that build on what was previously stated. そのうえ (on top of that / moreover) stacks additional facts; さらに (furthermore / even more) indicates an increase in degree or an additional development; しかも (moreover / and what is more) adds a piece of information that is surprising or particularly noteworthy.

spelling.text: 彼女は日本語が上手だ。そのうえ、英語も流暢に話せる。

definition: She is good at Japanese. On top of that, she can also speak English fluently.

spelling.text: ところで

patterns.title: ところで — by the way / incidentally
definition: A sentence-initial conjunction used to shift to a new topic unrelated to what was just being discussed. Unlike ところが (unexpected reversal within the same topic), ところで completely changes the subject, similar to 'by the way' or 'incidentally' in English.

spelling.text: 「昨日の映画、面白かったね。」「そうだね。ところで、今週末は何か予定ある？」

definition: 'Yesterday's movie was interesting, wasn't it.' 'Yeah. By the way, do you have any plans this weekend?'

spelling.text: ところが・それなのに

patterns.title: ところが・それなのに — however / and yet
definition: Adversative conjunctions expressing an unexpected reversal of what was expected. ところが (however / but then) objectively describes a surprising turn of events; それなのに (and yet / even so) carries a stronger emotional nuance of dissatisfaction or implied reproach toward someone for not meeting expectations.

spelling.text: 試験は難しいと思っていた。ところが、意外と簡単だった。

definition: I thought the exam would be difficult. However, it turned out to be surprisingly easy.

spelling.text: つまり・すなわち

patterns.title: つまり・すなわち — in other words / namely
definition: Sentence-initial conjunctions that restate or clarify what was just said. つまり (in other words / so) is neutral-to-casual and suitable for both speech and writing; すなわち (namely / that is to say) is formal and used in academic or legal prose to signal an exact equivalence.

spelling.text: 彼は毎日遅刻する。つまり、時間管理が苦手なのだ。

definition: He is late every day. In other words, he is bad at managing his time.

spelling.text: は vs が

patterns.title: は vs が — topic marker vs subject marker
definition: は marks the topic (theme, given/known information, contrast), while が marks the subject (new information, exhaustive focus, neutral description). The choice between them depends on what is foregrounded information in the discourse and produces significant differences in meaning and nuance.

spelling.text: 「誰が来ましたか。」「山田さんが来ました。」

definition: 'Who came?' 'Yamada-san came.' (が marks new information in the answer)

spelling.text: 謙譲語

patterns.title: Humble Language (Kenjougo)
definition: Honorific speech that lowers the speaker's (or in-group's) actions to indirectly show respect toward the listener or a superior.

spelling.text: 明日、先生のお宅に伺います。

definition: I will visit your home tomorrow, Sensei. (humble)

spelling.text: 尊敬語

patterns.title: Respectful Language (Sonkeigo)
definition: Honorific speech that elevates the subject (the listener or a third party) to show respect for their actions or state.

spelling.text: 先生はもうお帰りになりましたか。

definition: Have you (the teacher) already gone home?

spelling.text: 丁寧語

patterns.title: Polite Language (Teineigo)
definition: Polite speech that shows courtesy toward the addressee through です, ます, and ございます endings — it neither elevates nor lowers the subject of the sentence.

spelling.text: 今日は天気がいいですね。

definition: The weather is nice today, isn't it? (polite です)
